# Chain-hold on budget-window exhaustion: hold ~60s for the free-tier window to roll over (not hold 0s)

discovered-from: herdr-1792387482-2237208-25455 (audit of SA-0MVECQUGF0064U81, 2026-10-19)

## Problem (measured)

When a fallback chain exhausts because the `munitoai-free` sliding-window
request budget is momentarily full, the chain-hold wrapper holds **0s** and
fails all 3 cycles instantly, even though recovery is only the 60s window rollover
away. Audit Phase-2 (`audit-SA-0MVECQUGF0064U81-phase2_deep-ede9d520`) hit
`Pi provider error: "All providers exhausted"` twice + a failed verdict re-ask;
the verdict re-ask only succeeded minutes later once the window freed.

Proxy log (2026-10-19 ~07:23 local):

```
Rate limit exceeded for munitoai-free: 13/11 requests in 60s window
Provider budget exhausted: skipping provider=munitoai-free limit=11 reserve=4 remaining=2 reason=rate_limited
All providers exhausted for model=v1/chat/completions; unavailable={}; usage_limit_reset=None
Chain exhausted for model=v1/chat/completions; holding 0s before restarting cycle ...
```

Root cause chain:

1. Local Qwen3 saturated (0/2 slots held by other sessions) → queue 120s → fallback.
2. `plan.priority_routes.low = [local-qwen3, munitoai-free]` only; budget skip is a
   **pre-check** that never adds a cooldown entry → exhaustion response has
   `unavailable={}` (no cooldown, no usage_limit_reset).
3. `_bounded_hold_seconds` (LP-0MU56ZKQD005SX08) sees `retry_after <= 0` → returns
   **0.0** → `_run_chain_cycles` replays all `chain_hold_max_cycles` (3) cycles
   inside the same exhausted window → instant failure.

## Goal (user story)

As the proxy operator, when a chain exhausts solely because a free-tier rolling
budget window is full (cooldown-free, `unavailable={}`), I want the chain-hold
wrapper to hold ~the window rollover (bounded by existing budgets) so the next
cycle can succeed once the window frees — instead of failing all cycles
instantly and surfacing a spurious "All providers exhausted" to clients.

## Desired change

- When a budget-skip exhaustion carries no cooldown/`usage_limit_reset` but the
  entry has a `rate_limit_rpm` window, derive a `retry_after` from the window
  rollover (≤ the configured wait bounds, e.g. `provider_rate_limit_wait_max_seconds`)
  so `_bounded_hold_seconds` returns a positive hold instead of 0.0.
- Keep the "truly-retryable-now" case (real 0 cooldown) at 0s — no added latency.
- Respect `chain_hold_total_seconds` / client 900s ceiling.

## Acceptance criteria

- **AC1** — A chain whose only blockers are rate-limit budget skips yields a positive
  hold (~window rollover, subject to configured caps) rather than 0s, and the next
  cycle succeeds once the window frees (regression test modelled on the 13/11 scenario).
- **AC2** — Genuine instant-recovery exclusions (`retry_after == 0` from a real
  cooldown) still retry with no added latency (LP-0MU56ZKQD005SX08 behaviour preserved).
- **AC3** — Cumulative hold stays within `chain_hold_total_seconds` and strictly
  below the client's 900s deadline (LP-0MV6BR3HI00957PF contract).
- **AC4** — The 503 exhaustion body carries an accurate `Retry-After`/`retry_after`
  derived from the window rollover so clients can back off correctly.

## References

- Code: `proxy/proxy/provider.py` — `_run_chain_cycles` (~5809), `_bounded_hold_seconds`
  (~5686), `_log_chain_hold_start` (~5600); budget skip in `provider_budget.py`.
- Related items: LP-0MSH94Z7K007VKC9 (chain-hold origin), LP-0MU56ZKQD005SX08
  (hold bounded by retry_after — the 0.0 branch this item fixes), LP-0MVDUN5CY009VD20
  (free-tier reserve + 15s wait for in-progress sessions; new sessions pass through),
  LP-0MVDQ1GMO00801PL (do not over-use munitoai-free), LP-0MVDNP36J006430L (upstream
  x-ratelimit reset headers — complementary, cooldown based).

data.description:
## Problem statement

The proxy's `low` priority route (used by the priority-window cheap slot, 01:00–10:00 local, plus any explicit `X-Priority: low`) currently chains as `[local-qwen3, munitoai-free]` for the plan/author/code models. When the 2 local slots are saturated (a common overnight condition — see the 2026-10-19 proxy-usage-analysis report: `fallback_after_queue` 1657, `large_context_bypass` 1530, `context_too_large` 3393), low-priority traffic falls straight through to `munitoai-free`, which is capped at **`rate_limit_rpm: 2`** and is the last entry in the chain — so once its tiny budget is spent the request has nowhere else to go but an upstream 429 (16 upstream 429 events in the last window, all from `api.munito.ai`).

Meanwhile the three `opencode-go` entries (`opencode-go-3`, `opencode-go-2`, `opencode-go`) sit idle despite being available during their off-peak UTC windows (`["00:00-01:00", "04:00-06:00", "10:00-00:00"]`, added by LP-0MSXPHTD9004DZ4P) — which are precisely the hours when the cheap priority window is active and local is most contended.

Goal: allow low-priority work to fall back to **all** opencode models while they are inside their permissible (`available_times`) windows, so local-slot overflow during cheap hours is absorbed by idle paid capacity instead of being rate-limited on the free tier.

## Operator decisions (recorded)

- **Do NOT widen `available_times`.** The existing off-peak windows stay exactly as they are; paid spend remains confined to them.
- **Allow all opencode models on the low chain**, gated by those windows — not just one entry.

## Context / constraints

- `priority_routes.low` for plan/author/code is `[local-qwen3, munitoai-free]` (`proxy/config.yaml`); `munitoai-free` carries `rate_limit_rpm: 2`.
- Each of plan/author/code defines three equivalent opencode entries: `opencode-go-3` (OPENCODE_3_API_KEY), `opencode-go-2` (OPENCODE_2_API_KEY), `opencode-go` (OPENCODE_API_KEY) — same gateway, same model `deepseek-v4.1-flash`, same windows.
- **Why all three is meaningful (not cosmetic):** per LP-0MSMBWB23009XYPW / LP-0MVCX0E2V001VB5N, rate-limit quarantine is keyed on the **API-key account** (`_usage_limit_account_key` = `api_key_env@endpoint`), *not* the shared gateway domain. A 429 on one entry therefore poisons only that account, so its sibling keys are still tried with their own independent quota — i.e. 3× rate-limit capacity.
- **Counter-caveat to document:** for *non-rate-limit* failures (5xx, stalls) same-gateway siblings ARE skipped as one failure domain (`_failure_domain_key` / `attempted_domains`), so the three entries do **not** multiply capacity during an opencode outage. That is correct behaviour and must be stated in the config comments so nobody expects 3× resilience.
- **UTC-vs-local alignment (measured):** `available_times` are **UTC**; the cheap window (01:00–10:00) is **local `Europe/Dublin` = UTC 00:00–09:00**. opencode-go is unavailable UTC 01:00–04:00 and 06:00–10:00, so the new tiers add capacity in **~3 of the 9 cheap hours** (UTC 00:00–01:00 and 04:00–06:00). Accepted — the gaps are deliberate paid-spend avoidance, and the operator chose not to widen them.
- The `compact` model's low chain (`opencode-go-compact → deepseek-flash-compact`) is out of scope.
- The fully-paid `munitoai` and `deepseek-flash` entries must NOT join the low chain — they have no window discipline enforcing off-peak-only spend (`munitoai` has no `available_times` at all).

## Scope

Config + routing documentation + tests only. No llama-server changes, no `available_times` changes. Evidence via the proxy-usage-analysis skill (`python3 .pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/scripts/analyze_proxy_usage.py --hours 24`).

## Acceptance criteria

1. `priority_routes.low` for plan, author and code chains **all three** opencode entries, ordered after `munitoai-free`: `[local-qwen3, munitoai-free, opencode-go-3, opencode-go-2, opencode-go]`.
2. Every `available_times` value in `proxy/config.yaml` is **unchanged** by this work (no widening) — verifiable by diffing the config for `available_times` lines.
3. Unit tests prove window gating: inside a window the opencode entries are eligible; outside, they are skipped and the chain falls through exactly as today.
4. Unit tests prove per-key 429 failover: a 429 on `opencode-go-3` does not exclude `opencode-go-2`/`opencode-go` from the same request (independent account quota), while a 5xx on `opencode-go-3` DOES exclude them as one failure domain.
5. Chain order preserved: `local-qwen3` first when local has capacity; `munitoai-free` before any paid entry; `medium`/`high` chains byte-identical to before.
6. `munitoai` and `deepseek-flash` never appear in a `low` chain.
7. Config comments (and `priority.py::priority_routing_profile` docstring if it states the paid-tier invariant) document: the off-peak exception, the 3-of-9-hour UTC/local overlap, the per-key-429 capacity rationale, and the same-domain 5xx caveat.
8. Full suite passes via `/skill:test`; a post-change proxy-usage-analysis report is recorded on this item showing whether `rate_limited`/HTTP 429 from `api.munito.ai` fell during the overlap hours, with an honest "too small a sample" statement if not.

## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **LP-0MVF1FQJR000NH2I** – Add opencode-go to low-priority routes (off-peak) (blocked)
- **LP-0MVF1FM9500070U1** – Test: off-peak low-priority fallback gating (open)
- **LP-0MVBJXZY5002UW10** – start-proxy.sh auth.json key lookup does not match the documented munitoai-free name (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `proxy/proxy/provider.py` — matched: 0msmbwb23009xypw, 0mvcx0e2v001vb5n, 5xx, acceptance, accepted (+187 more)
- `proxy/README.md` — matched: 5xx, accepted, account, active, add (+181 more)
- `ds4/gguf-tools/imatrix/dataset/rendered_prompts.txt` — matched: acceptance, accepted, account, active, add (+175 more)

## Key Files (predicted)

- `proxy/config.yaml` — set `priority_routes.low` for `plan` (line 410), `author` (line 528) and `code` (line 653) to `[local-qwen3, munitoai-free, opencode-go-3, opencode-go-2, opencode-go]`; add the off-peak-window exception, per-key-429 capacity and same-domain-5xx caveat comments. Every `available_times` line must stay byte-identical.
- `proxy/proxy/priority.py` — `priority_routing_profile` (line 270) docstring: record the off-peak paid-tier exception where the paid-tier invariant is stated.
- `proxy/proxy/provider.py` — reused read-only: `_is_within_allowed_window` (line 2376, UTC window gate), `_usage_limit_account_key` (line 4358, per-account 429 quarantine), `_failure_domain_key` (line 4245, same-gateway 5xx skip).
- `proxy/tests/` — new window-gating, chain-order, per-key-429 and same-domain-5xx tests (owned by LP-0MVF1FM9500070U1).

## Effort and risk

- **Effort: S** — config edit + doc comments + tests; no new routing mechanism (`_is_within_allowed_window` already gates the chain).
- **Risk: Low** — window gate makes the change behaviour-neutral outside the off-peak windows; append-only chain change, fully reversible by removing three list entries.
- Recorded at the plan stage; the intake review changed no scope, so the estimate stands.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

Recorded from the `plan` session (comment `LP-C0MVF1G18A000NAJ0`), re-confirmed during this intake review.

### Q1. Which opencode-go entry joins the low chain?
`proxy/config.yaml` defines three equivalent entries: `opencode-go-3` (`OPENCODE_3_API_KEY`), `opencode-go-2` (`OPENCODE_2_API_KEY`), `opencode-go` (`OPENCODE_API_KEY`) — same gateway, same model `deepseek-v4.1-flash`, identical `available_times`.
**Answer (operator):** all three, ordered `opencode-go-3 → opencode-go-2 → opencode-go`, after `munitoai-free`. Rationale: rate-limit quarantine is per API-key account (`_usage_limit_account_key`, `proxy/proxy/provider.py:4075`), so sibling keys carry independent quota → 3× rate-limit capacity. Evidence: comment `LP-C0MVF1O13P001N6RO`.

### Q2. UTC vs local window alignment — widen `available_times`?
`available_times` are **UTC**; the priority cheap window (01:00–10:00) is local `Europe/Dublin` = UTC 00:00–09:00. opencode-go is unavailable UTC 01:00–04:00 and 06:00–10:00 → the new tiers add capacity in ~3 of 9 cheap hours (UTC 00:00–01:00, 04:00–06:00).
**Answer (operator):** do **not** widen the windows; paid spend stays confined to the existing off-peak windows and the 3-of-9 overlap is the accepted benefit. Evidence: `proxy/config.yaml` `available_times` (added by LP-0MSXPHTD9004DZ4P); comment `LP-C0MVF1O13P001N6RO`.

### Q3. Should the `compact` model's low chain change?
`compact` already chains `low: [opencode-go-compact, deepseek-flash-compact]` (`proxy/config.yaml` ~line 658) — no local tier, opencode already leads.
**Answer (eng):** no — out of scope, leave untouched.

### Q4. Do the fully paid `munitoai` / `deepseek-flash` entries join the low chain?
**Answer (operator/eng):** no. They carry no window discipline enforcing off-peak-only spend (`munitoai` has no `available_times` at all). Pinned as AC6.

### Duplicate-work check (this intake run)
`wl search` on `opencode-go`, `off-peak`, `low priority`, `priority_routes`, `munitoai` reviewed. Nearest neighbours: LP-0MSXPHTD9004DZ4P (added the off-peak windows — prerequisite, completed), LP-0MVDT94F0003VHUA (introduced priority routing with `low = local + free`, completed), LP-0MSMBWB23009XYPW / LP-0MVCX0E2V001VB5N (per-account quarantine — basis for AC4, completed). **No duplicate:** no existing item adds opencode-go entries to a `low` chain.

Two neighbours worth cross-referencing (neither duplicates this scope):

- **LP-0MVF0N9SA0071LWM** (in progress) — chain-hold on `munitoai-free` 60s budget-window exhaustion holds 0s and fails the chain instantly. Adding windowed opencode entries after `munitoai-free` gives the chain somewhere else to go, but does not replace the hold fix; sequence independently, no shared file beyond `provider.py` chain iteration (read-only here).
- **LP-0MVELM2NN006I0AU** (completed, `test-failure`) — legacy fast/cheap-mode assertions in `proxy/tests/test_priority_routing.py` / `test_provider_fallback.py` were rewritten for priority routing. The new gating tests (LP-0MVF1FM9500070U1) should extend those post-rewrite tests, not the removed fast-mode expectations.

### AC coverage review (this intake run)
`run_coverage_review(LP-0MVF17VP70053JXX)` → `recommendation: proceed` — all 8 acceptance criteria are covered by the three children (test LP-0MVF1FM9500070U1, config LP-0MVF1FQJR000NH2I, live verification LP-0MVF1FTPQ005ZMYO); no gaps, no conflicts.

# Reduce `munitoai-free` request budget to 2/minute

## Goal (user story)

As the proxy operator, I want the `munitoai-free` provider entry to dispatch at
most **2** requests per rolling 60-second window (down from 15), so the free tier
is used sparingly and traffic spills to the paid tiers rather than burning the
quiet free allowance on bursts.

## Scope

- `proxy/config.yaml`: `rate_limit_rpm: 15` → `rate_limit_rpm: 2` on all three
  `munitoai-free` entries (plan / author / code).
- Docs that quote the shipped value: `proxy/docs/routing.md` (ships-with value +
  value history), `proxy/README.md` (reserve arithmetic `11 of 15`).
- No change to the gate, reserve, wait caps or any other provider.

## Notes

- With `rate_limit_rpm: 2` and `provider_rate_limit_reserve_ratio: 0.3`,
  `floor(2 × 0.3) = 0` reserve slots, so new and in-progress sessions both see a
  cap of 2 per window (the reserve clamps to `rpm - 1`).
- Takes effect on the next proxy restart.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. All three `munitoai-free` entries in `proxy/config.yaml` declare
   `rate_limit_rpm: 2`.
2. `proxy/docs/routing.md` and `proxy/README.md` state the shipped value of 2 and
   describe the resulting reserve/cap arithmetic correctly.
3. The changed-scope test gate passes (config-loading / fallback-chain tests).
4. Commit recorded on this work item and pushed to `dev`.

## Goal

Pin the off-peak-windowed, all-opencode low-priority fallback behaviour with tests **before** the config change (test-first).

## Scope

Tests only; no production behaviour change in this item.

## Work

1. **Window gating:** an `available_times`-carrying entry is skipped outside its UTC window (`_is_within_allowed_window` → `Skipping provider=...: outside its available_times window (UTC)`) and selected inside it.
2. **Chain order:** `priority_routes.low` for plan/author/code resolves to `local-qwen3 → munitoai-free → opencode-go-3 → opencode-go-2 → opencode-go`. (Red until the config item lands — intended TDD state; document the convention if the repo requires green main.)
3. **Per-key 429 failover (the key behaviour):** a 429 from `opencode-go-3` must NOT exclude `opencode-go-2` / `opencode-go` from the same request — rate-limit quarantine is keyed on `_usage_limit_account_key` (`api_key_env@endpoint`), so sibling accounts are independent (LP-0MSMBWB23009XYPW, LP-0MVCX0E2V001VB5N).
4. **Same-domain 5xx caveat:** a 5xx from `opencode-go-3` DOES exclude its same-gateway siblings as one failure domain (`_failure_domain_key` / `attempted_domains`, LP-0MSG45I8Q0020N1F) — assert the honest behaviour so nobody assumes 3× outage resilience.
5. **No paid-tier leak:** `munitoai` and `deepseek-flash` never appear in any `low` chain.
6. **Medium/high unaffected:** those chains are unchanged.

## Acceptance criteria

1. Tests cover in-window selection, out-of-window skip-and-fall-through, and behaviour-neutrality when the free tier still has budget.
2. A test asserts the exact 5-entry low chain order for plan, author and code.
3. A test asserts 429-per-account failover lets sibling opencode keys be tried in the same request.
4. A test asserts 5xx does NOT give sibling failover (same failure domain).
5. A test asserts `munitoai` / `deepseek-flash` absent from `low` chains and `medium`/`high` chains unchanged.
6. Reuses existing proxy test conventions (monkeypatched clock for `available_times`, existing timing-gate fixtures) rather than inventing new harness code.
7. full suite green via `/skill:test`, except the documented intentional red chain-order assertion pending the config item.

## Goal

Let `low`-priority requests fall back to **all** opencode models while they are inside their permissible `available_times` windows, so local-slot overflow during cheap hours is absorbed by idle paid capacity instead of being rate-limited on the 2-rpm free tier.

## Operator decisions

- **Do not widen any `available_times`** — the existing off-peak windows are the paid-spend boundary and stay byte-identical.
- **Allow all opencode models** on the low chain, not just one entry.

## Background (measured)

- `low` chain today (plan/author/code): `[local-qwen3, munitoai-free]`, with `munitoai-free` at **`rate_limit_rpm: 2`** and last in the chain → overflow has nowhere to go but an upstream 429.
- Three opencode entries per model, same gateway/model, each with its own key: `opencode-go-3` (`OPENCODE_3_API_KEY`), `opencode-go-2` (`OPENCODE_2_API_KEY`), `opencode-go` (`OPENCODE_API_KEY`), all with `available_times: ["00:00-01:00", "04:00-06:00", "10:00-00:00"]`.
- Window-closed entries are skipped with `continue` (`provider.py`, ~line 2079), so appending them after `munitoai-free` is behaviour-neutral outside the windows.
- **429 failover is per API-key account** (`_usage_limit_account_key` = `api_key_env@endpoint`; LP-0MSMBWB23009XYPW, LP-0MVCX0E2V001VB5N) → the three entries give genuine 3× rate-limit capacity.
- **5xx/stall is per failure domain** (`_failure_domain_key`, LP-0MSG45I8Q0020N1F) → siblings are skipped as one domain during an outage; not 3× resilience. Document this.
- **UTC/local overlap:** `available_times` are UTC; the cheap window (local `Europe/Dublin` 01:00–10:00) = UTC 00:00–09:00; opencode unavailable UTC 01:00–04:00 and 06:00–10:00 → ~3 of 9 cheap hours gain capacity. Accepted.

## Work

1. Set `priority_routes.low` for `plan`, `author`, `code` in `proxy/config.yaml` to:
   `[local-qwen3, munitoai-free, opencode-go-3, opencode-go-2, opencode-go]`
   (free tier still preferred before any paid entry; the three opencode keys ordered as they appear in the `providers` lists so cache affinity matches the medium/high hot path).
2. Change **no** `available_times` value anywhere in the file.
3. Update the `priority_routes` block comment: the off-peak exception, the 3-of-9-hour UTC/local overlap, the per-key-429 rationale, and the same-domain-5xx caveat.
4. Update `priority.py::priority_routing_profile`'s docstring if/where it asserts "low never spends on paid tiers" so it states the off-peak-gated exception.
5. Leave `medium`/`high` chains, `compact`, `munitoai` and `deepseek-flash` untouched.

## Key files

- `proxy/config.yaml` — `models.plan/author/code.priority_routes.low` + comments
- `proxy/proxy/priority.py` — `priority_routing_profile` docstring
- `proxy/proxy/provider.py` — read-only reference for `_is_within_allowed_window`, `_usage_limit_account_key`, `_failure_domain_key`

## Acceptance criteria

1. `priority_routes.low` for plan, author and code is exactly `[local-qwen3, munitoai-free, opencode-go-3, opencode-go-2, opencode-go]`.
2. `git diff proxy/config.yaml` contains **zero** changed `available_times` lines.
3. `medium` and `high` chains are byte-identical to before; `munitoai` and `deepseek-flash` appear in no `low` chain.
4. Outside the windows the resolution order and behaviour are identical to today (proved by the test item).
5. `proxy/config.yaml` parses via `yaml.safe_load`; full suite passes via `/skill:test`.
6. Comments/docstring record all four rationale points (off-peak exception, 3-of-9 overlap, per-key-429 capacity, same-domain-5xx caveat).

Prove on real traffic that the all-opencode off-peak low chain absorbs local-slot overflow, and that it neither widens paid spend outside the windows nor regresses the free tier.

4. Confirm the three opencode keys each received traffic (i.e. per-key failover actually engages) by counting dispatches per `entry=` — `opencode-go-3` / `opencode-go-2` / `opencode-go` map one-to-one to `OPENCODE_3_API_KEY` / `OPENCODE_2_API_KEY` / `OPENCODE_API_KEY`. The log line carries `entry=`, not `api_key_env=`.
5. Comment the parent item (LP-0MVF17VP70053JXX) with the before/after table and verdict, and mirror the table on this item.

## Observation window

- Config change LP-0MVF1FQJR000NH2I was activated live at **2026-10-19T14:43Z** via `POST /admin/reload-config` (no proxy restart, no llama-server change); the 5-entry low chain has been in effect since.

- Sample-size caveat: the baseline window contained only 13 low-priority sessions, so a single night's post-change sample may be too small to move aggregate rates — report the effect size with that caveat rather than claiming a verified improvement.

- AC4: Per-key dispatch counts (`entry=opencode-go-3` / `opencode-go-2` / `opencode-go`) show whether more than one opencode key was used; if only one was used, say whether that reflects no 429s or an unexpected exclusion bug.

data.description:
# Intake Brief: Per model context size

**Headline:** Extend the fallback provider definitions with an optional
per-entry context-size limit (`max_context_tokens`) so a request whose
estimated prompt context exceeds a context-limited / rate-limited model's
allowance is skipped and the chain falls through to the next provider —
keeping oversized prompts away from tiers whose per-minute token budget they
would exhaust.

## Problem statement

Today the only context-size gates in the proxy are **local-model** thresholds
(`local_large_context_warm_cache_threshold`,
`local_large_context_cold_cache_threshold`, `local_model_ctx_size`, and the
hard routing cap in `proxy/router.py`). Remote provider entries
(`munitoai-free`, `munitoai`, `opencode-go*`, `deepseek-flash`, …) have **no
per-entry context ceiling**: every request, however large, is dispatched to the
first eligible provider in the chain.

For rate-limited tiers whose allowance is expressed in tokens per minute (the
MunitoAI endpoint advertises `x-ratelimit-*`; one large prompt can consume most
of a per-minute window — see LP-0MVBHDNLB007ALLJ), dispatching an oversized
request either triggers an upstream 429 or spends the whole window on one
request, pushing legitimate traffic onto paid tiers. Operators want the
fallback definitions to express a per-model context size so oversized requests
skip that entry.

## Users

- **Proxy operator** — wants per-tier context ceilings so rate-limited free
  tiers only ever receive requests sized within their allowance.
- **Pi agent sessions** running large-context tasks — should not stall on a
  rate-limited model that cannot (or should not) accept the request.

### User stories

- As the proxy operator, I want each provider entry to declare a maximum
  context size (`max_context_tokens`) so that a request above that size falls
  through to the next provider instead of being dispatched to a rate-limited
  model whose per-minute token budget it would exhaust.
- As a proxy operator tuning the MunitoAI free tier, I want to cap the free
  tier at a context size it can serve efficiently, so its small per-minute
  allowance is spent on several small requests rather than one huge one.

## Existing state

- **Local gates** in `proxy/provider.py`: `_should_skip_local()` implements the
  `context_too_large` hard cap (`local_large_context_warm_cache_threshold`,
  shipped `100000`) and the economic cold-cache bypass
  (`local_large_context_cold_cache_threshold`, shipped `38000`);
  `_get_active_local_ctx_size()` + `effective_per_slot_threshold()` clamp the
  warm cap to `local_model_ctx_size // slots - 4096`.
- **Hard routing cap** (`proxy/router.py`, `check_hard_routing_cap` /
  `compute_hard_routing_cap`) rejects over-cap requests *before* dispatch.
- **Remote gating today** is failure/availability based only: `resolve_provider()`
  and `_resolve_provider_with_exclusions()` skip entries on cooldown, shared
  failure domain, pending usage-limit reset and `available_times`; the
  capacity-aware request budget (`rate_limit_rpm`, `proxy/provider_budget.py` +
  `proxy/rate_limiter.py`) skips an entry when its rolling **60-second request**
  window is spent.
- **No per-entry context/token field exists** for any provider entry. Remote
  provider fields are parsed ad hoc in the chain loops
  (`_proxy_with_remote_fallback_cycle`, `_proxy_with_fallback_cycle`).
- In the chain loops the routing token estimate is currently computed **only
  inside the local branch**; the remote dispatch path (`acquire_provider_budget`
  → `ptr_remote`) never estimates prompt size.
- `munitoai-free` ships `rate_limit_rpm: 2`; `munitoai` (paid) is ungated.

## Desired change

Add an optional integer provider-entry field (working name
`max_context_tokens`) that caps the estimated prompt context an entry may
serve. Before dispatching to any provider entry, compare the request's
estimated prompt tokens (authoritative routing estimate) against the entry's
limit; when exceeded, **skip** the entry and fall through to the next eligible
provider. A skip is a per-request size mismatch, **not** a provider failure:
it must not apply a cooldown, usage-limit quarantine or failure-domain
exclusion, and it must never enter the contention queue.

The gate is **stateless per request** (see Assumptions) — it is not a rolling
tokens-per-minute accumulator.

## Acceptance criteria

- Provider entries in `proxy/config.yaml` accept an optional integer `max_context_tokens` (working name; final name confirmed before implementation) defining the maximum estimated prompt context the entry may serve. Absent, `0`, or non-positive = disabled (behaviour byte-for-byte as today).
- In both fallback dispatch loops (`_proxy_with_remote_fallback_cycle` and `_proxy_with_fallback_cycle`), an entry whose `max_context_tokens` is exceeded by the request's estimated prompt tokens is skipped **before** `acquire_provider_budget`/dispatch, and the chain proceeds to the next eligible provider.
- The skip is recorded as a request attempt (new status such as `provider_context_exceeded`) carrying the estimated tokens and the entry limit, and logged with the provider name, estimate, limit and reason.
- The estimate reuses the existing authoritative routing pipeline (`_get_tokenizer_for_model` + `_estimate_effective_prompt_tokens_for_routing` + `token_estimate_multiplier`) so the per-entry gate is consistent with the local gates and the hard routing cap. The estimate is computed once per request (or once per remote attempt) without a duplicate tokenizer pass per provider where avoidable.
- A skip is **not** a failure: it must not set a cooldown, record a usage-limit reset, add a failure-domain exclusion or record affinity for the entry; the entry remains eligible for later, smaller requests within the same chain cycle where routing allows.
- The gate is queue-safe: a context-exceeded skip never enters the contention queue and never triggers remote → local re-routing beyond the ordinary next-provider step.
- Local providers keep the existing `_should_skip_local` behaviour; if `max_context_tokens` is set on a local entry it composes as an **additional hard cap** (effective cap = `min(existing local thresholds, max_context_tokens)`) and never loosens the existing gate.
- Shipped `proxy/config.yaml` sets a documented, sourced `max_context_tokens` on each remote provider entry whose upstream model or rate allowance has a meaningful ceiling — at minimum `munitoai-free`, `munitoai`, the `opencode-go*` entries and `deepseek-flash` — with the value's source (upstream context window / provider per-minute token allowance) recorded in a config comment.
- Tests (new `proxy/tests/test_provider_context_limit.py`, plus extensions to `proxy/tests/test_provider_fallback.py` / `proxy/tests/test_munitoai_fallback_chain.py`) cover, with meaningful assertions: (a) an entry above its limit is skipped with the correct reason; (b) an entry at or below its limit is dispatched; (c) absent/`0` limit is ungated; (d) a skip falls through to the next provider; (e) no cooldown/affinity/usage-limit state is applied after a skip; (f) local chains are unaffected; (g) config-parsing of the new field.
- All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, the provider-entry field table in `proxy/MODEL_ADD.md`, `proxy/README.md` and `proxy/docs/routing.md` (field semantics + skip behaviour table).
- Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Constraints

- **Single authoritative config**: `proxy/config.yaml` only. Mode overlay files
  were removed with priority-based routing (LP-0MVDT94F0003VHUA) — do not
  reintroduce an overlay.
- **Backward compatible**: an absent field must be a no-op; no config schema
  break; existing chains must route identically when the field is unset.
- **No new cooldown/affinity side effects** (AC5).
- **Estimate reuse**: do not add a full tokenizer pass per provider entry if it
  can be computed once per request; the routing estimate is model-scoped, not
  provider-scoped.
- **Naming**: `max_context_tokens` is a working name; `context_size` /
  `max_prompt_tokens` are acceptable alternatives. Pick one and use it
  consistently across config, code, logs and docs.
- **Values**: shipped limits must be sourced (upstream model context window or
  the provider's documented per-minute token allowance), not guessed; if a
  value cannot be sourced, leave the entry ungated and record an open question
  rather than invent one.

## Risks & mitigations

- **Chain exhaustion / 503 regression** — all entries capped below a large
  request could exhaust the chain. *Mitigation:* leave at least one tier
  ungated (or set its limit to the largest upstream context window); AC8 and
  AC9(d) cover the fall-through path.
- **Estimate cost / tokenizer duplication** — estimating prompt size for every
  remote attempt could add latency. *Mitigation:* compute once per request and
  reuse (AC4).
- **Inconsistent estimate vs the local gate** — a different estimator would
  gate the same request differently per provider. *Mitigation:* reuse the
  existing authoritative pipeline (AC4).
- **Config drift / duplicated literal values** — same limit repeated across
  `plan`/`author`/`code` chains. *Mitigation:* document each value and its
  source; tests pin the resolved config (as `test_munitoai_fallback_chain.py`
  already does).
- **Scope creep** — a rolling tokens-per-minute accumulator, per-session token
  accounting, or dynamic limit derivation are **out of scope** (A1). Record
  them as linked follow-up work items rather than expanding this item.
- **Skip semantics mistaken for a failure** — applying a cooldown would
  unnecessarily remove a healthy tier. *Mitigation:* AC5 + AC9(e) assert no
  cooldown/affinity/usage-limit state after a skip.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `proxy/config.yaml` — add `max_context_tokens` to each remote provider entry;
  document the sourced value in a comment.
- `proxy/provider.py` — add a limit reader (e.g. `_provider_context_limit`)
  and a gate helper (e.g. `_should_skip_provider_context`); enforce it in
  `_proxy_with_remote_fallback_cycle` and `_proxy_with_fallback_cycle` before
  `acquire_provider_budget`; record the attempt with the new status.
- `proxy/router.py` — reconcile the hard routing cap / local branch so the
  shared estimate can be reused by the remote gate (no behaviour change to the
  existing cap).
- `proxy/observability.py` — register the new skip reason if it is added to the
  backend-signal / skip-reason counters.
- `proxy/tests/test_provider_context_limit.py` (new), `tests/test_provider_fallback.py`,
  `tests/test_munitoai_fallback_chain.py` — unit + integration coverage.
- `proxy/MODEL_ADD.md`, `proxy/README.md`, `proxy/docs/routing.md` — provider
  field table, semantics and skip-behaviour table.

## Related work

- **LP-0MVDQ1GMO00801PL** — Do not over-use MunitoAI-free (request-budget gate,
  `rate_limit_rpm`). This item adds the complementary *context-size* gate.
- **LP-0MVF19DKR008VCHO** — Reduce `munitoai-free` `rate_limit_rpm` to 2.
- **LP-0MVBHDNLB007ALLJ** — Honour MunitoAI `x-ratelimit-*` headers when queuing
  429 cooldowns (open; token/request allowance source of truth).
- **LP-0MU466L1X003RTHN** — Auto-derive large-context routing thresholds
  (local-only physical clamp + economic ceiling).
- **LP-0MSAZXXDY005AWA1** — `models.ini [global] ctx-size` / per-slot clamp.
- **LP-0MSF8XDG7000PERM** — `context_too_large` warm-cache threshold.
- **LP-0MVE0LUXN004PCO0** — `munitoai-free` `rate_limit_rpm` 24 h check-in.
- Docs: `proxy/docs/routing.md` (free-tier budgets, large-context bypass),
  `proxy/MODEL_ADD.md` (provider entry fields), `proxy/README.md`.

## Assumptions

- **A1 — stateless per-request gate.** The title/description mechanism
  ("define a per model context size … if the context goes above that size then
  fall through") is implemented as a per-request context-size comparison against
  a configured per-entry limit. The motivating "per minute token limit" is the
  reason for the ceiling, not a requirement to accumulate dispatched tokens over
  a rolling window. A rolling tokens-per-minute accumulator would be a separate
  feature; if required, file it as a follow-up item.
- **A2 — field applies to any entry.** The field is honoured on any provider
  entry; its primary target is remote tiers. On a local entry it acts as an
  extra hard cap (AC7).
- **A3 — skip is not a failure.** No cooldown/affinity/usage-limit state is
  recorded for a context-exceeded skip (AC5).
- **A4 — shipped values are sourced.** Limits are derived from public model
  context windows / documented provider allowances; unsourced values are left
  unset rather than guessed.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

No clarifying question was routed to the producer for this intake: the seed
context (title + description) states the mechanism explicitly — a per-model
context size in the fallback definitions, with requests above it falling
through to the next model — so the brief was drafted directly from the seed
plus repository research, as permitted by the intake skill ("Skip the
interview when the seed context suffices to draft a clear brief"). Recorded
research/traceability entries follow.

- **Q (self-resolved): Does a per-provider context-size field already exist?**
  — Answer: No. Research: inspected `proxy/config.yaml` provider entries,
  `proxy/provider.py` (`resolve_provider`, `_should_skip_local`,
  `_proxy_with_remote_fallback_cycle`, `_proxy_with_fallback_cycle`),
  `proxy/provider_budget.py` and `proxy/rate_limiter.py`; the only
  context-size gates are local-model thresholds and the hard routing cap.
  Source: repository inspection (2026-10-19).
- **Q (self-resolved): Is this a duplicate of prior work?** — Answer: No. The
  closest items are LP-0MU466L1X003RTHN (local-only large-context thresholds,
  completed) and LP-0MVDQ1GMO00801PL (`rate_limit_rpm` request budget,
  completed); neither implements a per-provider *context-size* gate for remote
  entries. Source: `wl search` + `wl show` (comment recorded on the item).
- **Q (self-resolved): Which provider entries are rate/context limited?** —
  Answer: the MunitoAI free tier (`munitoai-free`) is request-rate limited
  (`rate_limit_rpm: 2`) and its endpoint advertises `x-ratelimit-*` including
  token variants (LP-0MVBHDNLB007ALLJ); the `opencode-go*` and `deepseek-flash`
  entries carry `available_times` windows. Source: `proxy/config.yaml`,
  LP-0MVBHDNLB007ALLJ.
- **OPEN QUESTION (for implementation, not blocking intake): exact per-entry
  limit values.** The shipped values must be sourced from upstream model
  context windows / the provider's documented per-minute token allowance
  (AC8). If a value cannot be sourced, leave the entry ungated and raise it
  with the producer rather than guessing.
- **OPEN QUESTION (advisory): field name.** `max_context_tokens` (working
  name) vs `context_size` vs `max_prompt_tokens`; the implementer picks one and
  applies it consistently (Constraints).
## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **LP-0MTVMX58Y007J13F** – F2: Model-scoped failure-domain key implementation (completed)
- **LP-0MSG45LOO007K236** – Fix stall circuit breaker brand/entry key mismatch: cooldown never blocks opencode-go entries (completed)
- **LP-0MSG6IN80005JL4Q** – Implement failure-domain key + same-domain exclusion in fallback resolution (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `ds4/gguf-tools/imatrix/dataset/rendered_prompts.txt` — matched: absent, ac4, ac5, ac7, ac8 (+375 more)
- `ds4/gguf-tools/imatrix/dataset/rendered_prompts_think.txt` — matched: absent, ac4, ac5, ac7, ac8 (+375 more)
- `ds4/gguf-tools/imatrix/dataset/rendered_prompts_nothink.txt` — matched: absent, ac4, ac5, ac7, ac8 (+374 more)

## Implementation summary (shipped)

- Field: `max_context_tokens` (optional int, per provider entry); skip status `provider_context_exceeded`.
- F1 `LP-0MVF9MY0W002J2N3` tests (commit `753b535f`); F2 `LP-0MVF9N2QL001CDA7` gate (commits `ff7d81ec`, `2f922ab9`); F3 `LP-0MVF9N31A0006VH5` sourced shipped limits (commit `09ec8be4`); F4 `LP-0MVF9N3BV00155RI` docs + `backend_signals.provider_context_exceeded` counter (commit `c2a10cf6`); F5 `LP-0MVF9N3M7009Z8Q5` full-suite green gate (verification only).
- An absent/`0` limit is a no-op; a local entry's limit composes as `min(existing local thresholds, max_context_tokens)`; `github-primary` is deliberately ungated (no sourceable ceiling — see the F3 OPEN QUESTION).
- Verified green at `f7015f35` (full suite 4308 passed, 15 skipped).
## Audit chain

The parent audit ran in in-main-slot mode: each child's AC screens were serviced by the invoking session and the resulting child audit (verdict + per-AC evidence) was persisted on the child item, so a parent re-run reuses the stored child verdicts instead of re-screening them.

# Spend the full monthly OpenCode Go allowance before it resets (quota-aware surge)

## Goal (user story)

As the proxy operator, I want the proxy to steer more traffic to `opencode-*`
provider entries in proportion to the monthly allowance each account still has
and how close its reset is, **and to remove the `available_times` restrictions on
any `opencode-*` entry that still has allowance during the final week before its
reset**, so that each monthly Go/Go Plus allowance is fully spent (ideally
finishing on the last day) instead of expiring unused.

## Problem / background

OpenCode Go allowances are **use-it-or-lose-it**: usage limits are defined as
monthly dollar amounts per model, with a rolling-5-hour window at 20% of the
monthly cap and a weekly window at 50% (`https://opencode.ai/docs/go`). Any
allowance still unspent at `resetsAt` is simply lost — no carry-over.

Today the proxy is blind to how much of that allowance is left:

- `available_times` (LP-0MS4ETBNO0022QAC) gates every `opencode-go*` DeepSeek
  entry to the **off-peak** UTC windows (`00:00-01:00`, `04:00-06:00`,
  `10:00-00:00`) purely for pricing reasons, regardless of whether the account
  is sitting at 5% or 95% of its monthly cap.
- Routing order inside the `opencode-go*` chain is static; three accounts
  (`OPENCODE_API_KEY`, `OPENCODE_2_API_KEY`, `OPENCODE_3_API_KEY`) are tried in
  config order with no awareness of which one has allowance left.
- The proxy only learns about exhaustion **reactively**, from a
  `GoUsageLimitError` / 429 body (`proxy/provider.py:4363`,
  LP-0MSLJPOCC0001ROJ, LP-0MUQTCMW2001VXH8). The bug fixed in
  LP-0MUQTCMW2001VXH8 was triggered by guessing reset times; a proactive,
  authoritative reading removes the guesswork entirely.

Consequence today: a key can finish a monthly period at 88% (observed, below)
while another sits at 5%, and the residual allowance on every key expires
unspent at the end of each period.

## Discovery findings (verified live 2026-10-19 ~10:22–10:25 UTC)

Facts established by probing the gateway directly with the existing keys; the
implementation should not need to re-derive these.

1. **Response headers carry no quota information.** `POST
   https://opencode.ai/zen/go/v1/chat/completions` returns only `date`,
   `content-type`, `content-length`, `cf-placement`, `x-opencode-log-id`,
   `x-zen-model`, `server`, `cf-ray`. No `x-ratelimit-*`, no `retry-after`, no
   reset hints, on success **or** on error. Response body `usage` carries token
   counts only — no cost/price/remaining figures.
2. **The authoritative quota source is `GET https://opencode.ai/zen/go/v1/usage`**
   (Bearer key, no `x-opencode-session` needed, `cache-control: no-store`):

   ```json
   {"usage":{"rolling":{"status":"ok","percent":0,"resetsAt":"2026-10-19T15:22:54.000Z"},
             "weekly":{"status":"ok","percent":0,"resetsAt":"2026-10-26T00:00:00.000Z"},
             "monthly":{"status":"ok","percent":88,"resetsAt":"2026-10-23T08:43:55.000Z"}}}
   ```
3. **Quota is per API key (per account), not per model, and the endpoint takes no
   model selector** — `?model=…` and `?detailed=true` are silently ignored and
   return the same aggregate. The per-model dollar limits documented on the Go
   page are therefore not observable through this API.
4. **Live readings at time of writing** (shows the problem concretely — two of
   three accounts are close to exhaustion, one is nearly untouched):

   | entry | `api_key_env` | rolling | weekly | monthly | monthly `resetsAt` |
   |---|---|---|---|---|---|
   | `opencode-go` | `OPENCODE_API_KEY` | 0% | 0% | **88%** | 2026-10-23T08:43:55Z |
   | `opencode-go-2` | `OPENCODE_2_API_KEY` | 0% | 0% | **95%** | 2026-10-30T00:03:43Z |
   | `opencode-go-3` | `OPENCODE_3_API_KEY` | 3% | 1% | 5% | 2026-11-17T10:05:09Z |
5. **Reset dates are per account and are not calendar-aligned** (the three keys
   reset 7 days apart), so the surge window must be computed per account from its
   own `resetsAt`, not from a fixed calendar rule.
6. `rolling.resetsAt` behaves like "end of the current 5-hour window"
   (≈ now + 5 h) rather than "unblock time"; the `weekly.resetsAt` is
   week-aligned.
7. **Peak vs off-peak pricing matters for quota burn rate**: DeepSeek V4.1 Flash
   is $0.15/$0.60 per 1M tokens off-peak and $0.30/$1.20 peak (peak hours
   `01:00-04:00` and `06:00-10:00` UTC, Mon–Fri). Because the monthly allowance
   is a *dollar* amount, tokens spent in peak hours deplete it twice as fast.
8. Model IDs: `opencode-go` serves only `deepseek-v4.1-flash` and
   `deepseek-v4-pro`; `deepseek-v4-flash` exists only on the plain `deepseek`
   provider. Requests need an `x-opencode-session` header (the proxy already
   synthesises it, `tests/test_opencode_session_header.py`).
9. There are **no** `/v1/credits`, `/v1/billing`, `/v1/quota`, `/v1/me` or
   `/v1/account` endpoints (all 404). The console-only "Use balance"
   pay-as-you-go fallback is not API-visible — see the cost guard below.

## Requirements

- **R1 — Quota poller.** Poll `GET /v1/usage` per distinct `api_key_env` on a
  configurable interval, cache the result, de-duplicate concurrent polls per
  account, and fail open (keep the last known values, log at WARN) on error,
  timeout or malformed JSON.
- **R2 — Derived state.** From each poll derive, per account: `monthly_headroom =
  100 - monthly.percent`, `weekly_headroom`, `rolling_headroom`,
  `seconds_to_reset`, and an `exhausted` flag. The **effective headroom is the
  minimum of the three windows** — the monthly cap is irrelevant if the 5-hour
  or weekly window is already spent.
- **R3 — Headroom-aware ordering.** Within the `opencode-go*` chain, order
  eligible entries by descending quota urgency score
  (`effective_headroom / seconds_to_reset`, producer decision Q2 → 2c),
  stable tie-break on the existing config order, so traffic goes to the
  account that can absorb it most before its own reset. An
  entry whose effective headroom is below the exhaustion threshold is treated as
  unavailable for routing (same effect as a cooldown, but derived from quota
  rather than from a 429).
- **R4 — Final-week surge (removes date restrictions).** When
  `0 < seconds_to_reset <= quota_surge_days` (default 7) **and** the entry is not
  exhausted, `available_times` gating is bypassed for that entry: it becomes
  eligible at any UTC hour, and this is logged once per state change with
  `reason=quota_surge`. The bypass clears automatically when the entry becomes
  exhausted or when its reset passes.
- **R5 — Pacing that front-loads spend without stranding quota.** Within the
  surge window the dispatch preference must increase with remaining headroom and
  with diminishing time-to-reset, targeting roughly 100% consumption at
  `resetsAt` — but the ramp must be *achievable*, i.e. it must respect the
  rolling (20%) and weekly (50%) caps, because a large residual cannot be
  discharged in a last-minute burst. Surge must therefore start ramping before
  the final week whenever the residual is large, so the last day finishes the
  quota rather than trying to finish it all at once.
- **R6 — Prefer cheaper tokens first.** Surge ordering prefers windows that are
  already `available_times`-eligible (off-peak) and only uses peak hours when the
  residual is projected to be unspendable otherwise. Peak hours burn allowance at
  2x the rate (finding 7).
- **R7 — Hard stop / cost guard.** Never dispatch to an entry whose monthly
  `percent` is at or above `quota_exhaustion_percent` (default 99.5), and never
  after a `GoUsageLimitError`. This must hold *especially* if the account has the
  console "Use balance" option enabled, where over-consumption would spend real
  pay-as-you-go money. Surge bypasses **only** `available_times` — never
  `rate_limit_rpm`, the sibling-failure circuit breaker, failure-domain grouping
  or stall/quarantine gates.
- **R8 — Observability.** Log every poll, every surge enter/exit, every ordering
  decision and every quota-driven skip, at a level that fits the existing log
  volume (polls/transitions at INFO, per-request ordering at DEBUG). Expose the
  derived per-account quota state in the existing metrics/status surfaces so an
  operator can answer "how much is left, when does it reset, is surge active".
- **R9 — Off by default is not required, but a kill switch is.** Configuration
  must allow the whole behaviour to be disabled (`server.quota_surge_enabled:
  false`) and a dry-run mode that emits the routing decisions it *would* make
  without changing routing.
- **R10 — Documentation.** `config.yaml` documents every new key with its
  default, and `docs/dev/quota-surge.md` explains the pacing model, the peak/
  off-peak trade-off and the reset-alignment caveat.

## Acceptance criteria

- **AC1** — With a stubbed `/v1/usage` transport, the poller issues at most one
  request per account per `server.quota_poll_interval_seconds` (default 900 s)
  no matter how many client requests arrive, and concurrent pollers coalesce
  into a single in-flight request per account. A poll failure (500, timeout,
  malformed body) leaves the previous values intact, logs at WARN, and never
  fails or delays a client request.
- **AC2** — Derived state is exposed (metrics/status surface) as, per account:
  `rolling/weekly/monthly percent`, `resetsAt`, `seconds_to_reset`,
  `effective_headroom`, `surge_active`, `exhausted`. Verified by a test that
  feeds a known `/v1/usage` payload and asserts the exposed values, including
  that `effective_headroom` is the **minimum** of the three windows (feed
  `rolling=95, weekly=10, monthly=40` and assert effective headroom is 5).
- **AC3** — Given `opencode-go` at monthly 88% and `opencode-go-3` at 5% with
  both eligible, the routing decision prefers `opencode-go-3`. Reversing the
  percentages reverses the preference. Equal headroom falls back to config order
  (deterministic).
- **AC4** — An entry whose monthly `percent >= 99.5` (or effective headroom
  below the threshold) is skipped without any upstream request being attempted,
  and the skip is logged with the reason. Repeated over a table of window
  combinations.
- **AC5** — Final-week bypass: with `resetsAt` 6 days away and monthly 50%, an
  entry configured with `available_times: ["10:00-00:00"]` is eligible at a
  simulated 02:00 UTC (previously ineligible) and the eligibility is logged with
  `reason=quota_surge`. With `resetsAt` 8 days away the same entry at 02:00 UTC
  remains ineligible (unchanged behaviour).
- **AC6** — The bypass is scoped to `available_times` only: with surge active, an
  entry that is rate-limited (`rate_limit_rpm`), circuit-broken, or in a
  usage-limit quarantine is still skipped. Verified by a test that activates
  surge and simultaneously trips each of those gates.
- **AC7** — Pacing function is unit-tested over a table of
  `(effective_headroom, seconds_to_reset)` pairs and satisfies: (a) monotonically
  non-decreasing in headroom at fixed time-to-reset; (b) monotonically
  non-decreasing as reset approaches at fixed headroom; (c) returns the baseline
  (no-surge) preference outside the surge window; (d) a large residual with a
  near reset yields a higher preference than a small residual with a distant
  reset for the same entry; (e) never yields a preference that would exceed the
  rolling/w weekly cap in a single 5-hour window (asserted against the documented
  20%/50% relationship).
- **AC8** — With `server.quota_surge_enabled: false`, routing decisions are
  byte-identical to today's behaviour for a table of representative requests
  (existing `available_times` and ordering tests continue to pass unchanged). In
  dry-run mode the computed decisions are logged but routing is unchanged.
- **AC9** — A stale-quota guard: when the last successful poll is older than
  `server.quota_state_max_age_seconds` (default 3600 s), surge is suspended and
  the proxy reverts to configured `available_times` (fail-safe, not fail-open),
  logged at WARN.
- **AC10** — Hard stop: a simulated `monthly.percent = 99.6` (or a
  `GoUsageLimitError` response) mid-surge stops surge for that account on the
  very next dispatch decision, with zero further requests to that entry in the
  same test, and the existing quarantine path from LP-0MSLJPOCC0001ROJ still
  applies.
- **AC11** — Tests cover the poller, derivation, ordering, bypass, pacing, guards
  and kill switch (unit + at least one integration test against a fake upstream),
  all green, and the existing suite is unaffected.
- **AC12** — Documentation: `config.yaml` comments for every new key and
  `docs/dev/quota-surge.md` describing the model, the peak-pricing caveat and the
  per-account (non-calendar) reset dates.
- **AC13** — Post-deploy measurement: a log-derived report (reuse
  `.pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis`) shows, per account, the monthly percentage
  at the moment of reset for the first full period after deployment, and the
  target is ≥ 90% (the residual ≤ 10% being the safety margin needed for the
  rolling/weekly caps).

## Proposed approach (for the implementer to refine)

1. New module `proxy/quota_state.py`: async poller (httpx, shared client with the
   existing `server.remote_http_client` settings), per-account cache, injectable
   transport for tests (mirroring `_usage_limit_probe_transport`).
2. Wire the poller into startup/lifecycle and expose state through the existing
   metrics/status surfaces.
3. `proxy/provider.py`: extend eligibility (`_provider_in_available_window`,
   `proxy/provider.py:2378`) with a surge override, and extend chain ordering so
   `opencode-*` entries sort by effective headroom. Keep the change behind a
   single, well-named predicate so AC8's "unchanged when disabled" is easy to
   prove.
4. Config keys under `server` (defaults in brackets):
   `quota_surge_enabled` [`true`], `quota_surge_dry_run` [`false`],
   `quota_poll_interval_seconds` [`900`], `quota_surge_days` [`7`],
   `quota_exhaustion_percent` [`99.5`], `quota_state_max_age_seconds` [`3600`],
   `quota_pacing_target` [`0.95`] and an optional `quota_surge_accounts` filter
   (default: all `opencode-*` entries).
5. Optional (only if it falls out cheaply): reuse the derived
   `seconds_to_reset` to replace the *guessed* reset time in
   `_usage_limit_reset_info` for `GoUsageLimitError`, which would retire the
   guessing path from LP-0MUQTCMW2001VXH8 for these accounts.

## Non-goals / out of scope

- No change to the MunitoAI / DeepSeek-direct / GitHub chains (the same idea may
  later apply to `munitoai`, which does expose `x-ratelimit-*` headers —
  LP-0MVDNP36J006430L / LP-0MVBHDNLB007ALLJ).
- No console/credit-balance API integration (none exists, finding 9).
- No per-model quota tracking (not observable, finding 3).
- Not a replacement for the existing reactive 429/`GoUsageLimitError` handling —
  it complements it.

## Risks and guards

- **Overspend risk** if a "Use balance" pay-as-you-go fallback is enabled on the
  console side → mitigated by R7/AC10 (hard stop below 100%) and by making the
  stop threshold conservative by default.
- **Peak-hour burn** → R6/AC7(e) prefer off-peak; document that surge can spend
  allowance ~2x faster per token during peak hours.
- **Blast radius on routing** → kill switch + dry-run (AC8) and the surge
  predicate scoped to `available_times` only (AC6).
- **Third-party API stability** → `/v1/usage` is undocumented on the Go page, so
  the poller must degrade gracefully (AC1) and the feature must remain safe if
  the endpoint disappears.
- **Stale state** → AC9 fail-safe revert.
- Money-relevant changes should be reviewed by the operator before merge.

## Assumptions (documented per project convention)

1. `opencode-go`, `opencode-go-2`, `opencode-go-3` (and any future `opencode-*`
   entry) are all in scope; surge applies per entry, keyed by `api_key_env`.
2. "Monthly allowance available" means `100 - monthly.percent`, additionally
   bounded by the rolling and weekly windows (finding 2 / R2).
3. The intent is to consume the *included* allowance, not to buy pay-as-you-go
   capacity — hence the hard stop at 99.5%.
4. Importing the surge mechanism must not change behaviour for non-`opencode-*`
   providers.
5. Exact `status` values beyond `"ok"` are unknown; the implementation must treat
   anything other than `ok` conservatively (blocking) rather than optimistically.

## Related work items

- LP-0MS4ETBNO0022QAC — timed access (`available_times`), whose restriction this
  item selectively relaxes.
- LP-0MSXPHTD9004DZ4P / LP-0MSCDOIT4008TBFQ — off-peak windows for
  opencode-hosted DeepSeek (the windows this item overrides during surge).
- LP-0MSLJPOCC0001ROJ — `GoUsageLimitError` quarantine with computed reset.
- LP-0MUQTCMW2001VXH8 — guessed usage-limit quarantine locking accounts for up to
  30 days (the failure mode proactive quota reading avoids).
- LP-0MVF1FQJR000NH2I / LP-0MVF17VP70053JXX — blocked/open items about routing to
  `opencode-go` during off-peak windows (ordering interaction to check when
  implementing).
- LP-0MVDQ1GMO00801PL — per-provider request budget (`proxy/provider_budget.py`),
  the gate surge must not bypass.

## Open questions (resolved during planning)

1. Spend profile → **RESOLVED (option 1a):** keep defaults — 95% pacing target,
   99.5% hard stop, AC13 target ≥ 90% at reset. Before merge the operator should
   still confirm the console "Use balance" option is OFF on all three accounts
   (Q2 below), per the money-relevant-change review rule.
2. Is the console "Use balance" option enabled on any of the three accounts?
   **STILL OPEN — operational check for the producer** (hard stop and threshold
   defaults would be tightened if enabled on any account).
3. Surge ordering tie-break → **RESOLVED (option 2c):** score =
   `effective_headroom / seconds_to_reset`; equal/missing inputs fall back to
   config order (R3 amended; AC3's determinism wording retained).
4. Do org-scoped keys (`X-Opencode-Org-Id` appears in the endpoint's CORS
   allow-list) change the meaning of `/v1/usage` percentages? **STILL OPEN**, no
   impact on planning (not used by any plan feature).


## Plan (decomposed 2026-10-19)

Ten child features, each a vertical slice ending in tests, created in
dependency order. Test-first: the poller slice lands the shared fake-`/v1/usage`
test harness every later feature is built through; the integration/regression
slice is deliberately last.

| # | Child work item | Covers | Depends on |
|---|---|---|---|
| F1 | Quota poller and derived state (tracer bullet) (LP-0MVF7KEG7007C8MF) | AC1, AC2 (derivation), R1/R2 | — |
| F2 | Pacing model: urgency score and cap achievability (LP-0MVF7KHI5000J7BL) | AC7, R5/R6 | F1 |
| F3 | Headroom-aware opencode chain ordering (LP-0MVF7KIKE002DZVD) | AC3, R3 | F1, F2 |
| F4 | Final-week available_times surge bypass (LP-0MVF7KJN2000ASE8) | AC5, AC6, R4 | F1, F2 |
| F5 | Quota hard stop and cost guard (LP-0MVF7KO8C005NB59) | AC4, AC10, R7 | F1, F3 |
| F6 | Stale-state fail-safe, kill switch and dry-run (LP-0MVF7KPB9009U7CG) | AC8, AC9, R9 | F1, F4, F5 |
| F7 | Quota observability surface (LP-0MVF7KQED005TG9Z) | AC2 (exposure), R8 | F1, F4 |
| F8 | Configuration keys and quota-surge design doc (LP-0MVF7KRH30000KOA) | AC12, R10 | F2–F6 |
| F9 | End-to-end integration test and regression gate (LP-0MVF7KSJW007L2QF) | AC11 | F3–F7 |
| F10 | Post-deploy allowance-utilisation measurement (LP-0MVF7KTMI005B667) | AC13 | F9 |

Out of scope but tracked: Retire guessed usage-limit reset for opencode
accounts (LP-0MVF7MPZN009GOJB) — producer decision Q3 → 3a, follow-on task
blocked on this epic shipping.

Vertical slices are enforced per feature (code + tests + config key + log lines
in each). Between phases, review the next item's description and update it
(pacing/score parameters, observed log volume) before implementing.

### Plan: changelog
- 2026-10-19: decomposed into 10 features + 1 follow-on item; R3 amended to
  urgency scoring per producer decision 2c; open questions 1 and 3 resolved.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q: "Spend target profile — (a) keep defaults 95% target / 99.5% hard stop /
  AC13 ≥90%; (b) tighter 90%/99.0%; (c) aggressive 99%/99.9%?" Answer
  (producer): "1. A". Final: keep defaults. Evidence: session
  herdr-1792407026-3930919-14977 reply "1. A 2. C 3. A".
- Q: "Ordering tie-break — (a) headroom then config order; (b) headroom then
  nearest reset; (c) score = headroom / seconds_to_reset?" Answer (producer):
  "2. C". Final: score = `effective_headroom / seconds_to_reset`; equal scores
  fall back to config order (stable). R3 amended accordingly.
- Q: "Include reusing `/v1/usage` seconds_to_reset to retire the guessed
  `_usage_limit_reset_info` path (parent proposal item 5)?" Answer (producer):
  "3. A". Final: out of scope for the epic; tracked as follow-on
  LP-0MVF7MPZN009GOJB.
- Q (operational, still open): is the console "Use balance" option enabled on
  any of the three accounts? Directed to the producer; matters because it would
  tighten the hard stop / threshold defaults before merge.

# Remove stale REFACTOR markers when their work item closes

## Problem statement

The refactor skill injects `REFACTOR-<id>` marker comments into source files to suppress duplicate work-item creation, but there is no removal path: once the referenced smell is fixed (or judged a false positive) and its work item closes, the marker persists and — because `has_existing_comment(file_path, smell_type)` matches on *smell type* only — permanently suppresses detection of that smell type in that file.

## Users

- **Implementation agents** running `/skill:refactor` or the implement pipeline's refactor step — they trust duplicate suppression to be accurate; a stale marker silently hides a real regression.
- **Developers reading source files** — stale markers are noise that misrepresents outstanding work.
- **Producers triaging the Refactor backlog** — a closed work item should leave no trace in the codebase.

Example user stories:

- "As an agent running the refactor step, when a marker's work item is already closed, I want the marker gone (or ignored) so I do not skip a smell that has regressed."
- "As a developer, when a refactor item is completed or judged a false positive, I want its comment removed from the file without touching surrounding code or line endings."
- "As a producer, I want a single command that reports every stale marker in the project and can clean them up."

## Existing state

- `skill/refactor/comment_injection.py` provides `inject_refactor_comment()`, `has_existing_comment()`, `get_comment_style()` and `_build_comment_block()`; there is **no removal function**.
- Two slightly different regexes parse markers: `comment_injection.REFACTOR_PATTERN` (`REFACTOR-(\S+).*?smell:\s*(\S+)`, DOTALL) and `workitem_creation.REFACTOR_COMMENT_PATTERN` (multi-line, expects a comment prefix before `smell:`).
- Markers are written in two shapes: line-prefixed (`# <!-- REFACTOR-…` … `# -->` for Python/YAML/shell, `// <!-- …` for JS/TS) and native block (`<!-- … -->` for Markdown/HTML). CSS-family files use `/* … */` with ` * ` prefixes.
- `inject_refactor_comment()` reads and writes text mode without `newline=""`, so injected files are normalised; removal must not repeat that mistake.
- `StatusLifecycle.show()` and `shared.status_lifecycle.resolve_worklog_flags()` already provide safe work-item lookup and prefix-to-sibling worklog-store resolution. Verified: a bare `wl show <foreign-prefix-id>` fails ("Work item not found"), so a sweep **must** inject `--worklog-dir` from the shared resolver.
- `skill/refactor/scripts/refactor.py` `remediate_pre_existing()` injects markers only for smells it just filed items for; the pipeline syncs the worklog first (`wl sync --if-idle`) and has no post-close hook.
- The canonical source of the skill is `~/projects/SorraAgents/skill/refactor/` (symlinked into `~/.pi/agent/skills/refactor`); its tests live in `~/projects/SorraAgents/tests/test_refactor/`, with `tests/test_refactor/test_comment_injection.py` (1251 lines) covering the current API.
- Stale markers confirmed at HEAD in the `llm` repo (work-item state checked 2026-10-20):

| File | Marker | Item stage |
|---|---|---|
| `.pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/tests/test_analyze_proxy_usage.py:2` | `REFACTOR-LP-0MVDFQC2X005S7WE` | open / `intake_complete` — reported false positive |
| `.pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/tests/test_analyze_proxy_usage.py:8` | `REFACTOR-LP-0MTHLGVPO004DZ56` | completed / `done` |
| `proxy/tests/test_compaction_config.py:2` | `REFACTOR-LP-0MTGDB3D9007TWHA` | completed / `done` |
| `proxy/tests/test_cold_start_immunity.py:2` | `REFACTOR-LP-0MVB0THT7000KT0G` | completed / `done` |
| `proxy/tests/test_compaction_logger_hierarchy.py:2` | `REFACTOR-LP-0MTV87EC4006EU5Z` | completed / `done` |
| `proxy/proxy/router_helpers.py:2` | `REFACTOR-LP-0MTRWI65I005VXOC` | completed / `done` |
| `proxy/proxy/provider.py:2` | `REFACTOR-LP-0MSI4ZIF60064EOR` | completed / `done` |

- The same defect is visible in the `SorraAgents` repo itself: `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py` (2 markers), `pi-client/voice-input/whisper_worker.py`, `skill/audit/tests/test_audit_json_contract_reask.py` (3), `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py` (2), `skill/standup/tests/test_generate_standup_regressions.py` — 4 of these reference `completed` items, the rest reference `open / idea` items.

## Desired change

1. **Removal API** in `skill/refactor/comment_injection.py`: `remove_refactor_marker(file_path, work_item_id) -> dict` (or a small dataclass) that locates the whole marker block for that id — line-prefixed, `<!-- -->` and `/* */` shapes — and deletes it, leaving the remainder of the file byte-identical (including CRLF/LF and the file's original trailing newline). Absent marker → `{"removed": False, "reason": "absent"}`; repeated runs are no-ops.
2. **Sweep module** (new `skill/refactor/marker_sweep.py`): discover markers in repo-tracked files (exclude `.worklog/`, `node_modules`, binaries), group by referenced work-item id to one `wl show` per distinct id (worklog dir resolved via `shared.status_lifecycle.resolve_worklog_flags`), classify each marker as `stale` (stage `in_review`/`done`/`completed` or status `completed`), `active` (any other resolved stage) or `unknown` (lookup failed), and return a structured report.
3. **Trigger** from the refactor pipeline: run the sweep after the `wl sync` and **before** smell detection, so `has_existing_comment` never observes a stale marker. Non-fatal on `wl` failure (log a warning, keep markers). Standalone CLI entry point (`--sweep-markers`, report-only by default, `--apply` to delete) and a skip flag (`--no-marker-sweep`).
4. **`has_existing_comment` correctness**: keep it a pure file predicate by default, but accept an optional `is_active` resolver/callback so a caller can exclude terminal items; the pipeline's sweep-before-detect ordering is what makes the default path correct. `unknown` markers keep suppressing (conservative) and are reported as warnings.
5. **False-positive path**: a marker whose item is still open but was judged a false positive must be removable explicitly (`--remove-marker <work-item-id>` or `remove_refactor_marker()` called directly), independent of item stage.
6. **Unit tests** in `tests/test_refactor/`: removal for `#`, `//`, `<!-- -->` and `/* */` shapes; block and line-prefix styles; CRLF preservation; absent-marker no-op; idempotent re-run; multi-marker file touching only the target block; classification of `in_review`/`done`/`completed`/`open`; `unknown` id kept and reported; dry-run performs no writes; cross-store id resolution.
7. **Sweep the existing stale markers** in `llm` (6 stale; the false positive needs an explicit decision) and in `SorraAgents` (4 stale), so `grep -rn "REFACTOR-"` afterwards shows only markers whose items are non-terminal.
8. **Documentation**: `skill/refactor/SKILL.md` (§ REFACTOR Comments + flags table + report keys), `docs/refactor.md` (§ 4 Work Item Creation, troubleshooting "Duplicate work items created", module reference), and module docstrings. `CHANGELOG.md` is excluded (ship pipeline owns it).

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `remove_refactor_marker()` removes a `REFACTOR-<id>` marker block (line-prefixed, `<!-- -->` and `/* */` styles) from a file while leaving all surrounding content byte-identical and preserving the file's line endings (verified by a CRLF fixture test).
- [ ] Removal is a no-op (`removed=False`) when the marker is absent, and re-running it is idempotent.
- [ ] A sweep reports every marker in the project with its referenced item's stage and a classification of `stale` / `active` / `unknown`; removal is triggered for markers whose work item is at a terminal stage (`in_review`, `done`, `completed`).
- [ ] Sweep work-item lookups resolve the correct worklog store via the shared resolver (a foreign-prefix id resolves; failure is non-fatal and keeps the marker as `unknown`).
- [ ] `has_existing_comment()` no longer suppresses detection for closed work items — covered by a test asserting a terminal-stage marker is not treated as an existing comment on the sweep-before-detect path (and via the optional active-item filter).
- [ ] An explicit false-positive removal path exists for markers whose work item is still open, with `--dry-run` making no writes.
- [ ] Running the sweep (apply mode) removes the 6 stale `llm` markers listed above and the 4 stale `SorraAgents` markers; a follow-up `grep -rn "REFACTOR-"` shows only markers whose items are non-terminal.
- [ ] Unit tests cover: `#`, `//`, `<!-- -->` and `/* */` styles; absent marker; idempotent re-run; multi-marker file; terminal vs non-terminal classification; unknown id; dry-run no-write.
- [ ] All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
- [ ] Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Constraints

- Canonical source is `~/projects/SorraAgents/skill/refactor/`; never edit `~/.pi/agent/skills/...` (the installer replaces it) and never hand-edit markers in `llm` outside an authorised implementation run.
- Standard library only — no new third-party dependencies.
- One `wl show` per distinct referenced work-item id (cached per run); the sweep must stay in the same sub-second-to-low-seconds envelope as the existing pipeline rather than spawning per marker.
- Sweep is read-only unless `--apply` (or the default pipeline policy) removes stale markers; `--dry-run` must never write.
- Never remove a marker for an item that is not terminal unless explicitly requested by id.
- Only scan git-tracked files in the repo root (skip `.worklog/`, worktrees, `node_modules`, binary files).
- Work-item ids may belong to sibling project stores; always route `wl` through the shared resolver, not the cwd default.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `~/projects/SorraAgents/skill/refactor/comment_injection.py` — add `remove_refactor_marker()`, a single tolerant marker parser covering both existing regexes, `is_active` filter hook on `has_existing_comment()`, and `newline=""` IO.
- `~/projects/SorraAgents/skill/refactor/marker_sweep.py` (new) — marker discovery, per-id work-item lookup via `shared.status_lifecycle`, classification and report structure.
- `~/projects/SorraAgents/skill/refactor/scripts/refactor.py` — sweep step after `wl sync` / before detection, `--sweep-markers`, `--apply`, `--remove-marker`, `--no-marker-sweep` flags, report keys.
- `~/projects/SorraAgents/skill/refactor/workitem_creation.py` — reuse the unified marker pattern instead of its own `REFACTOR_COMMENT_PATTERN`.
- `~/projects/SorraAgents/skill/refactor/SKILL.md` — marker lifecycle and new flags.
- `~/projects/SorraAgents/docs/refactor.md` — § 4, troubleshooting, module reference.
- `~/projects/SorraAgents/tests/test_refactor/test_comment_injection.py` — extend with removal tests.
- `~/projects/SorraAgents/tests/test_refactor/test_marker_sweep.py` (new) — sweep classification, dry-run, unknown ids, non-fatal wl failures.
- `llm`: `.pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/tests/test_analyze_proxy_usage.py`, `proxy/tests/test_compaction_config.py`, `proxy/tests/test_cold_start_immunity.py`, `proxy/tests/test_compaction_logger_hierarchy.py`, `proxy/proxy/router_helpers.py`, `proxy/proxy/provider.py` — sweep targets only (no hand edits).

## Risks & assumptions

- **Repository placement (assumption A1):** the skill's source of truth is `SorraAgents`, so the code change belongs there with its own `SA-` work item; this `LP-` item then owns the `llm` sweep. Risk: `implement.py` creates worktrees from the cwd's `.worklog`, so an `LP-` item cannot host edits under `~/projects/SorraAgents`. Needs producer confirmation (Q1).
- **No close hook:** `wl` exposes no plugin/hook on close (only `wl plugins` for discovery), so "triggered when the item reaches a terminal stage" is implemented as a sweep at refactor-run time plus a standalone command — not an event. Assumption A2.
- **False-positive regression loop:** removing the marker for a closed false-positive item re-enables detection, so the next scan re-files the same item. Mitigation: false positives must be closed with a reason *and* either fixed or excluded via `.refactor.json`/per-file ignore; the sweep should report (not silently hide) this case. Scope-creep risk — an ignore-list mechanism is a separate work item.
- **Mixed answers to `unknown`:** unresolvable ids (deleted items, wrong store) could hide real work. Conservative default: keep + warn.
- **Formatting churn:** a naive implementation strips a leading blank line or rewrites CRLF files, producing whole-file diffs. Byte-preserving IO (`newline=""`, explicit trailing-newline handling) plus a CRLF fixture test is mandatory.
- **Regex divergence:** the two existing patterns disagree on block styles; unifying them is required or Markdown/CSS markers will be missed by the sweep.
- **Scope creep:** generalising to a lifecycle framework for all agent-injected comments is out of scope; record as a separate item if it surfaces.

## Open questions

1. **Repository and work-item placement** — implement in `~/projects/SorraAgents/skill/refactor` under a new `SA-` item (this `LP-` item keeps the `llm` sweep and records the blocker), or keep everything under this `LP-` item and treat the SorraAgents edits as out-of-worktree?
2. **Trigger surface** — sweep automatically inside the refactor pipeline (default) plus a standalone `--sweep-markers --apply`, or standalone-only (manual/cron)?
3. **False positives and unresolvable ids** — should `has_existing_comment` keep suppressing on `unknown` ids (conservative) while a manual `--remove-marker <id>` handles false positives, or should both be dropped automatically?

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q: "Which repository should host the skill change — `SorraAgents/skill/refactor` (canonical source, its own `SA-` item) or this `LP-` item in `llm`?" — **OPEN QUESTION**. Research: `~/.pi/agent/skills/refactor` is a symlink to `/home/rgardler/projects/SorraAgents/skill/refactor`; the skill's tests live in `SorraAgents/tests/test_refactor/`; `implement.py` creates worktrees from the cwd's `.worklog`, so an `LP-` item cannot legally host edits under `SorraAgents`. **Recommended:** new `SA-` item in `SorraAgents` for the skill change, `LP-0MVF4OPC1001RYX6` scoped to the `llm` marker sweep and recording the blocker.
- Q: "How should the terminal-stage trigger be implemented, given `wl` exposes no close hook?" — **OPEN QUESTION**. Research: `wl plugins` only lists plugins; no event/hook surface found; the refactor pipeline already runs at the end of implementation and syncs first. **Recommended:** sweep inside the refactor pipeline (after `wl sync`, before detection) plus a standalone `--sweep-markers` report/`--apply` CLI.
- Q: "Should markers referencing unresolvable work items, and false-positive markers whose item is still open, be removed automatically?" — **OPEN QUESTION**. Research: all `llm` markers resolve today except none; `LP-0MVDFQC2X005S7WE` is open at `intake_complete` while the marker is documented as a false positive. **Recommended:** keep `unknown` markers and warn; require an explicit `--remove-marker <id>` for open-item false positives.

# Resolver stale-key comparison unit tests (RED)

## Goal

Pin the AC4 resolver-level behaviour with failing unit tests **before** any
implementation, following the AC-pinning test pattern of
LP-0MVBJXZY5002UW10 (see the `api_key_resolver` section of
`proxy/tests/test_restart_lifecycle.py`).

Part of LP-0MVD2RF7H008B7OT (start-proxy.sh stale-key detection). Test-first
child: authored before the resolver helper (sibling child) so the helper's
contract is executable, not prose.

## Scope

Extend the `api_key_resolver` test section in
`proxy/tests/test_restart_lifecycle.py` (per the parent's Key Files) with:

- `key_fingerprint()` tests: returns the first 8 characters; never returns the
  whole key for keys longer than 8 chars; returns `""` for `None`/empty.
- `compare_env_key(env_var, env_value, auth)` tests covering the four AC4
  cases:
  1. env var set **and matching** `auth.json` → status `match`, both
     fingerprints identical.
  2. env var set **and differing** → status `mismatch`, fingerprints differ,
     neither fingerprint is the full key.
  3. env var **unset** → status `resolved` (auth.json value returned for
     export).
  4. **auth.json missing** (pass `None` / unreadable) → status `auth_missing`
     (or the agreed equivalent), no exception raised.
- Additional pinned cases: env set + auth.json missing → `env_only` (keep env,
  warn, do not fail); `OPENCODE_API_KEY` still prefers `opencode-go` when
  comparing.
- `--check` CLI mode: exit 0 on match/resolved, exit 3 on mismatch, exit 4 on
  unresolved; stdout is JSON and contains **no plaintext key** when the env
  var is set.

## Constraints

- Fixture keys must be ≥ 12 characters (e.g. `MATCHING_KEY_AAAA`) so
  fingerprint redaction is actually exercised.
- No test may print or assert a full API key from a real `auth.json`; fixtures
  only, via `tmp_path`.
- Must not import the live proxy app or touch the network.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC4 (parent):** Test coverage: env-var-set-and-matching, env-var-set-and-differing (refuse/warn), env-var-unset (resolve from auth.json), auth.json missing — each of the four cases is represented by at least one named resolver-level test.
- `key_fingerprint()` is pinned: first 8 characters, never the whole key for keys longer than 8 chars, `""` for empty/`None`.
- `compare_env_key()` is pinned for all four AC4 cases plus env-set/auth.json-missing (`env_only`) and the `opencode-go` preference.
- The `--check` CLI contract is pinned: exit 0 for match/resolved, 3 for mismatch, 4 for unresolved; stdout carries fingerprints only when the env var is set.
- The new tests fail for the right reason (missing helper / missing CLI mode) before the implementation child lands; no existing resolver test changes behaviour.
- Test names state the AC they pin (traceability to parent AC1–AC4).

## Key Files

- `proxy/tests/test_restart_lifecycle.py` — extend the `api_key_resolver` section.
- `proxy/proxy/api_key_resolver.py` — imported read-only (contract target of the sibling child).

## Dependencies

None. Blocks the resolver helper and both start-proxy.sh children.
