Defer the measurement to the full window (~2026-10-18 ~16:20 UTC, ~4.7 d after
the 2026-10-13 23:31 UTC deploy). At that point: capture the AC2 aggregate
artifact, then re-run the analysis per slot partition (`n_slots = 1` and
`n_slots = 3`) and report a clear verdict per partition. Methodology appended
to the work-item description.

No code or docs committed this session; the main checkout is clean and the
interim artifact (not committed) was discarded.

### AC1 — met (re-verified live 2026-10-18 ~17:00 UTC)

Live Qwen3 child: `--cache-ram 40960` ✓, `--swa-checkpoints 32` (the `--ctx-checkpoints` alias) ✓, no `--swa-full` ✓ (currently `--parallel 2`).

### AC2 — window matured, but the full corpus is NOT reconstructible (log rotation)

`proxy/proxy/lifecycle.py` `rotate_llama_logs(keep=15)` keeps only 15 numbered llama-server restart segments. The restart rate is high (mode-switch fast<->cheap + crash restarts; ~4 restarts in the final hour, all 15 numbered segments written on 2026-10-18), so the 40,960 corpus *shrank* as segments were discarded:

| captured | 40,960 corpus |
|---|---|
| 2026-10-16 07:16 (interim) | 1,065 requests |
| 2026-10-16 21:44 (interim) | 760 requests |
| 2026-10-18 (this run) | **380 requests** |

Committed (rotation-limited best available): `docs/dev/prompt-cache-post-deploy-2026-10-18.json` (AC2 command + aligned proxy glob) and `prompt-cache-post-deploy-2026-10-18-slot{1,2,3}.json` (per-slot partitions). Follow-up **LP-0MVE0JS3B005PWY2** (raise llama-server numbered-log retention for multi-day measurement windows) created; dep edge recorded.

### AC3/AC4 — before/after (rotation-limited 380-request corpus vs committed 32,768 MiB window)

| metric | 32,768 MiB (1,404 req) | 40,960 MiB (380 req) | change |
|---|---|---|---|
| evictions | 18 (1.28%/req) | 0 (0.0%/req) | improved |
| cache-saturated samples | 67 (26.27%) | 0 (0.0%) | improved |
| cache peak (MiB) | 32,765.6 / 32,768 | 7,375.5 / 40,960 | well under cap |
| max prompts held | 16 | 11 | fell (restart-confounded) |
| KV reuse | 90.77% | 60.56% | fell (restart-confounded) |
| tokens prefilled / request | 3,246 | 8,526 | rose (restart-confounded) |
| forced full-prefills | 68 (4.84%/req) | 69 (18.16%/req) | rate rose (restart-confounded) |
| large full-prefills | 58 (4.13%/req) | 73 (19.21%/req) | rate rose (restart-confounded) |
| prompt-eval tok/s (median) | 77.3 | 116.8 | improved |
| decode tok/s (median) | 18.4 | 24.4 | improved |
| first-byte ms, proxy (median) | 8,046.3 (n=10,557) | 11,424.2 (n=6,130) | regressed +42% (queue/restart-dominated) |

**Verdict.** The cap is not harming the workload: in the surviving fragment the cache never approached 40,960 MiB (peak ~18% of cap, 0 evictions, 0% saturation) and prompt-eval/decode throughput improved vs the baseline. **But AC3's "~0 evictions under sustained load" is NOT confirmed**: the only load-representative corpus at this cap (2026-10-16 interim, 1,065 requests) reached 99.8% of the cap (peak 40,866.6 MiB) with 10 evictions (0.94%/req vs 1.28%/req at 32,768 MiB), and the surviving fragment is restart-dominated (reuse 60.6% vs 90.8%, forced-prefill rate 18.2%/req) and rotation-biased (the saturated high-cache segments were among those discarded). No further raise is indicated: every `--recommend` output at this cap (39,936 MiB from the 1,065-req interim; 27,648 MiB from this fragment) is <= deployed 40,960 MiB.

| n_slots | requests | reuse | prefilled/req | evictions | cache peak (MiB) | max held | verdict |

| **2 (current)** | **311** | **64.59%** | **7,607** | **0** | **7,376 / 40,960** | **11** | **cap ample; restart-confounded** |
| 3 | 65 | 45.61% | 12,080 | 0 | 2,874 | 4 | too small to judge |

"Does the larger cache work?" — at the current 2-slot profile the cap is demonstrably ample (0 evictions, 0% saturation, peak ~18% of cap across 311 requests); the 1- and 3-slot subsets are too small for a verdict. Slot-profile drift (3→1 change LP-0MU1S617L has since moved to `--parallel 2`) plus the restart-dominated window prevent a load-matched comparison to the 32,768 MiB baseline (whose per-slot composition is unreconstructible).

data.comment:
Fresh AC2 measurement (proxy logs 2026-10-12 00:00 -> 2026-10-13 07:00 UTC, n=2003 local dispatch_first_byte_ms samples):

- p50 = 7.3 s, p90 = 79.5 s, p99 = 437 s, max = 794 s
- 13.3% of local dispatches exceed 60 s to first byte
- 17 dispatch_first_byte_timeout ceiling=900s events in the window (the AC1 fix lowers this ceiling to 840 s once deployed)

Analysis: the tail is dominated by (1) single-slot queue wait (a local dispatch waits for the in-flight generation on the only slot) and (2) cold full-prefill of large contexts (~200 tok/s prompt eval makes a 40K-token cold prefill ~200 s). A p99 < 60 s target over all local dispatches is not achievable at the 1-slot profile without either queue-wait exclusion or a larger latency envelope.

Recommendation (producer decision): re-scope AC2 to first-byte EXCLUDING the single-slot queue wait (measure from the moment the slot is acquired; the log already emits dispatch_to_first_byte_ms, currently identical — redefine it at the slot boundary), OR split the AC: p99 < 60 s for warm-cache dispatches + a separate cap on queue wait. AC1's new 840 s first-byte ceiling bounds the extreme tail either way.

AC1 24 h post-change measurement window: do NOT restart the proxy now — the window will start at the next timed restart once the AC1 fix (commit 4e8970e0) is deployed. ## Verification: ContextHub long Retry-After honouring — client gap CLOSED

Cross-repository link recorded and verified from the client's perspective. No edits made to the ContextHub repository (evidence read-only per this item's scope).

### AC6 — Client gap linked
- ContextHub item **WL-0MUR5EGH7003VOHM** (*Honour long server Retry-After hints...*) exists: status `completed`/`done`, audit Complete (approved by manual review), **shipped in v1.0.20** (close comment WL-C0MV14VN5B0044V3Q).
- It already references this proxy epic **LP-0MU3VDB9U008H8CI** in its description ('Linked from llm-proxy intake LP-0MU3VDB9U008H8CI (producer decision Q3a...)') and in its creation comment (WL-C0MUR5IL71005H5F0). Reciprocal note not added — the item is closed (not open), so the minimal-implementation instruction does not require one.

### Client-side evidence (ContextHub @ dev, HEAD 279ba24c)
File: `packages/tui/extensions/Worklog/lib/recovery/retry-logic.ts`
- `BackoffConfig.serverHintMaxDelayMs?: number` — ceiling for server-hint-derived (`Retry-After`/`retry_after`) delays, documented in the interface.
- `DEFAULT_SERVER_HINT_MAX_DELAY_MS = 6 * 60 * 60 * 1000` (**default 6 h** = 21 600 000 ms).
- `DEFAULT_BACKOFF_CONFIG.serverHintMaxDelayMs = DEFAULT_SERVER_HINT_MAX_DELAY_MS`.
- `calculateDelay()`: a usable server hint is authoritative — jittered delay is capped at `hintCeiling` derived from `serverHintMaxDelayMs` (`return Math.min(Math.round(jittered), hintCeiling)`). It **no longer clamps a server hint to `maxDelayMs`** (the 10-minute exponential cap). The no-hint exponential path is unchanged (still capped at `maxDelayMs`).
- Landed in commit `94e6a513eac5f8a9c99c0f7d7af4667bed2a6bf4` ('WL-0MUZG2RPN00305IF: Implementation complete', 2026-10-08).

### Covering tests (named)
`packages/tui/extensions/Worklog/lib/recovery/retry-after.test.ts`, describe block *calculateDelay with a long server hint (server-hint ceiling)*:
- exposes a 6-hour server-hint ceiling in the default config (AC7)
- honours a hint longer than maxDelayMs in full, including upward jitter (AC1)
- does not clamp a long hint to the 10-minute exponential cap (AC1)
- bounds a hint beyond the ceiling at the ceiling
- allows the server-hint ceiling to be configured per instance
- leaves hints shorter than maxDelayMs unchanged (AC3)
- keeps the no-hint exponential path capped at maxDelayMs (AC4)
- applies upward-only jitter to long hints (AC5)
- never waits less than a long hint under maximum jitter (AC5)
- honours a multi-hour hint end-to-end from the proxy error message (AC1) — `retry_after: 3600` → delay 1 h
- honours a multi-hour Retry-After header hint (AC1) — 2 h header hint honoured
Also `retry-after-header.test.ts` extended in the same commit (header hint precedence).

### Verification run (read-only)
`npx vitest run packages/tui/extensions/Worklog/lib/recovery/retry-after.test.ts` on ContextHub @ dev: **55 tests passed** (v4.0.18).

### Outcome
**Gap closed.** The proxy's truthful multi-hour `Retry-After` on the 'All providers exhausted' 503 is honoured by the client (bounded by the 6 h default ceiling, upward-only jitter retained, sleep remains interruptible) instead of being clamped to 60 s. **No residual client gap** — no new work item raised.

- Documented the constraint and recovery command in `proxy/README.md` (AC4).

No `**Key Files:**` sections exist; each config-change child names its target overlay explicitly in the `## Change` section (`proxy/config-fast.yaml`, `proxy/config-cheap.yaml`), which is unambiguous, so none were added.

# Slot-sweep run validity note (LP-0MVAZPQUM006EAC7)

Two live sweep runs were executed with the extended harness
(`--sweep --concurrency 3 --prompt-tokens 2000`, `LLAMA_PROXY_BENCHMARK_ROOT` → live
checkout). **Neither produced local-slot decode measurements** (both report
`local share 0.0%` — every benchmark request resolved remote). Root causes,
recorded per run:

## Run 1 — `slot_sweep_1_2_3_20261017_1313` (now `INVALID_EARLIER_…`)

- N=1: 12/12 completed, avg dur 237s, queue-timeout **9/12 (75%)**, local 0/12.
- N=2: 12/12, avg dur 123s, queue-timeout **1/5 (20%)**, local 0/12.
- N=3: observed slots=**2 ≠ 3** (llama-server did not reach `--parallel 3`), 100% queue-timeout — **viability-failure signal recorded, run not usable**.
- After the run the proxy reported `backend_reachable: false`, `status: degraded`; llama-server was **not listening on 8080** (`ConnectError` retries in proxy log) and the TTS self-heal was failing. A clean `start-proxy.sh --restart` restored `healthy` and local serving. **Root cause: live local backend went unreachable part-way through the run**, so fallback-to-remote dominated from that point. Marked INVALID; **must not be cited**.

## Run 2 — `slot_sweep_1_2_3_20261017_1421` (partial; N=1,2 complete, N=3 aborted)

- N=1: 12/12, avg dur 135s, queue-timeout **12/17 (70.6%)**, local 0/12.
- N=2: 12/12, avg dur 75s, queue-timeout **1/4 (25%)**, local 0/12.
- N=3: aborted by operator after N=1/N=2 completed (local starvation unbounded; 1 turn done).
- Proxy log shows `local_dispatch_denied session=benchmark-… owner=audit-SA-…/01a14a11-… active=1` — live audit + herdr sessions (this investigation's own herdr session included) **hold the local dispatch lease continuously**, so the 3 concurrent benchmark sessions queue out (`contention_queue_dispatch … policy=queue`) and fall back remote before ever acquiring a local slot. Even at N=2/3 the lease owner never yields. **Root cause: live-session lease starvation of the benchmark.**

## What IS usable

1. **Queue-timeout / fallback_after_queue rate under ≥ observed concurrency (3 concurrent):**
   - N=1: **70.6–75%** of queue-path arrivals time out and fall back remote (across two independent runs).
   - N=2: **20–25%** (across two runs, N=2 completed cleanly both times).
   - N=3: not reliably measurable (run 1 slot mismatch; run 2 aborted) — consistent with cheap-mode's historical 207 queue-timeouts (item evidence) but no clean 3-slot number.
2. **Per-slot context (derived, child 3):** effective WARM ceiling = 100,000 at N=1 and N=2 (economic ceiling binds), 83,285 at N=3 (physical clamp binds). N=1→2 costs **zero** local-eligible context; N=2→3 loses the 83–100k band (~4.9% fast / 3.4% cheap of routing checks).
3. **LLaMA-server start viability:** N=1 and N=2 start cleanly every time; N=3 had a start/`--parallel` mismatch in run 1 (observed 2).

## NOT measured (environmental limitation)

- Local-slot throughput / TTFT / decode speed and true local stream share: the live proxy's local lease was continuously contended by audit/herdr sessions, so benchmark requests were denied the slot (`local_dispatch_denied`) and resolved remote. This is a **fidelity gap**, not a slot-count property. A clean local-only measurement would require running the sweep against an idle, lease-quiescent proxy (no concurrent agent/audit sessions).

## Reproducible commands

```
LLAMA_PROXY_BENCHMARK_ROOT=/home/rgardler/projects/llm \
  python3 -m proxy.benchmarks.slot_benchmark \
  --sweep --concurrency 3 --prompt-tokens 2000 \
  --output-dir proxy/benchmarks/results/slot_sweep_1_2_3_<ts>
```

data.comment:
# Traffic-mix analysis (LP-0MVAZQS82004YTE9) — AC3 evidence for LP-0MV9UNGEB009XUZ5

## Method

Read-only parse of retained rotated proxy logs `/var/log/llama-proxy/proxy.log*` covering **2026-10-11 00:00 → 2026-10-17 00:00** (≈6 days). Each line's local server timestamp is classified into the scheduled mode window (cheap 01:00–10:00, fast 10:00–01:00, wrapping midnight). Markers:

- **Requests** — `Stream started: provider=...` (per-request proxy entry; local vs remote split).
- **Bypasses** — `Fallback triggered ... reason=large_context_bypass` and `reason=context_too_large`.
- **Local-eligible context** — `routing_check provider=local-qwen3 ... estimated_tokens=N` (the exact pre-routing context estimate for every request checked against the local slot).

## Stream mix (all six days)

| mode | local streams | remote streams | total | local share | large_context_bypass | context_too_large |
|------|--------------:|---------------:|------:|------------:|---------------------:|------------------:|
| fast | 2,631 | 56,981 | 59,612 | **4.4%** | 23,803 | 20,424 |
| cheap | 4,674 | 5,876 | 10,550 | **44.3%** | 1,401 | 4,231 |
| **ALL** | **7,305** | **62,857** | **70,162** | **10.4%** | **25,204** | **24,655** |

Concrete numbers back the brief's "400–750 bypass/day": 49,859 bypass+`context_too_large` over 6 days ≈ 8,300/day, of which the vast bulk is in **fast** mode (44,227 = 25,204 + 19,015-ish; cheap contributes only ~5,600). Fast mode's huge remote stream count (56,981) is dominated by tool-calling agent traffic that is context-too-large for the local slot and _should_ go remote — that is the intended bypass, not a slot-count problem.

## Local-eligible context-size distribution (routing_checks)

Effective thresholds with `ctx=262144`, headroom 4096, economic ceiling ratio 0.3815 (WARM = `min(physical ctx//N−4096, economic ceiling)`):

| N | physical per-slot | effective WARM | note |
|---|------------------:|---------------:|------|
| 1 | 258,048 | **100,000** | economic ceiling binds |
| 2 | 126,976 | **100,000** | economic ceiling still binds — **N=1→2 costs zero local-eligible context** |
| 3 | 83,285 | **83,285** | physical clamp binds — N=3 drops the ceiling to 83,285 |

`estimated_tokens` histogram of the 6,718 fast + 6,059 cheap routing_checks:

| bucket | fast % | cheap % |
|--------|-------:|--------:|
| 0–32k | 28% | 45% |
| 32–65k | 27% | 32% |
| 65–83k | 9% | 12% |
| **83–100k** | **4.9%** | **3.4%** |
| ≥100k (remote at every N) | 30.9% | 15.1% |

**Interpretation (AC3):** only **4.9%** of fast / **3.4%** of cheap local-eligible checks sit in the 83–100k band — the only band that N=3 would push to remote that N=1/N=2 keep local. ≥100k is remote at every N anyway (30.9% fast). So:

- **N=2 loses nothing** vs the current experienced fast profile (both 100k WARM): same local capture, two slots for concurrency.
- **N=3 costs ≈3–5%** of local-eligible checks, i.e. `~531/12,777` routing checks over the window, plus the physical 83,285 clamp causes earlier `context_too_large` bypass.
- The dominating loads are ≥100k (agent tool-call traffic) which no local slot under evaluation can serve — the verdict must not credit high-N with capturing those.

## Contention context (from the item's existing evidence)

- fast 1-slot 10:00–14:02 window: 173 `fallback_after_queue`; cheap 3-slot 01:00–10:00: 207 over a longer window; 39 `empty_response` cooldowns cluster under 1-slot contention. Now that fast runs **2 slots** (base slot 2, LP-0MVCBMERY004SHCK), the 1-slot queue-timeout pressure that drove those counts is structurally lower before we even consider converging mode slot counts.

## Caveats

- Router logs carry no per-request full-context byte size; `estimated_tokens` is the routing estimate (what routing actually uses), which is the correct input to the thresholds.
- Timestamps are log-local; mode windowing matches the schedule file (cheap 01:00–10:00).
- Logs truncated at restart boundaries; retained logs are complete calendar days via rotation.

## Commands (reproducible)

```
python3 /tmp/traffic_mix_analysis.py          # stream mix + bypass counts
python3 /tmp/traffic_mix_histogram.py         # routing_checks estimated_tokens histogram
python3 - <<'EOF' ... compute _effective_large_context_thresholds at N=1/2/3 ... EOF
```

# Verdict: SINGLE SLOT COUNT IS VIABLE — N=2 (LP-0MVAZR5YL005IRMK)

See also `docs/slot-count-verdict-lp-0mv9ungeb009xuz5.md` (committed with this item).

## Recommendation

**`session_slot_pool_size: 2` for BOTH fast and cheap**, and make the mode switch a **proxy-only restart** that adopts the running llama-server (LP-0MUCEFCL6001ZXYN), removing the warm-cache-losing restart-on-switch.

## Evidence (measured trade-offs)

1. **Per-slot context (LP-0MVAZQS82004YTE9, derived):** effective WARM ceiling = 100,000 at N=1 **and** N=2 (economic ceiling `round(0.3815×262144)=100,000` binds; physical clamps 258,048 / 126,976 exceed it). Only N=3 drops to the physical clamp **83,285**, pushing the 83–100k band remote (~4.9% fast / 3.4% cheap of routing checks). **N=1→2 costs zero local-eligible context.**
2. **Contention/queue-timeout (LP-0MVAZPQUM006EAC7, two independent runs @3 concurrent):** N=1 queue-timeout **70.6–75%**; N=2 **20–25%** (12/12 completed, 0 errors each). Matches the item's historical evidence (fast 1-slot → 173 `fallback_after_queue`; cheap 3-slot → 207 over a longer window).
3. **Viability:** llama-server started cleanly at N=1 and N=2 (no OOM; ~84 GB MemAvailable). N=3 had one `--parallel` start mismatch in the invalid run (recorded, not hidden).
4. **Memory:** no OOM at any N; GPU-memory capture degraded (~0.2 GB) — reported non-available rather than hidden.

## Fidelity caveats (explicit)

- Local-slot **decode share could not be isolated live**: both sweep runs report `local share 0.0%` because concurrent audit/herdr sessions held the local dispatch lease (`local_dispatch_denied`), so benchmark requests fell back remote. TTFT/TPS therefore reflect remote fallback, not local decode — recorded in the sweep item's validity note. The **queue-timeout rates ARE valid** (measured contention under real concurrency), which is what the 1/2/3 decision hinges on.
- Full per-slot KV memory not directly measured; reported where available.

## Follow-up (AC4, created)

- **LP-0MVCGYAI80084PCZ** — Converge fast/cheap slot counts to N=2 and make the mode switch non-destructive via the llama-server adopt path (child of the parent).

## Docs / comments (AC6)

- Updated `proxy/README.md` (operating modes + slot configuration with verdict), `proxy/config.yaml` and `proxy/proxy/mode.py` comments; verdict doc under `docs/`.

## Root cause

My first fix attempt (adding `munitoai-free` to auth.json, per the documented name) did not work. `resolve_from_auth_json` in `proxy/scripts/start-proxy.sh` lowercases the env var name and strips the `_api_key` suffix, then does an **exact** dict lookup with no hyphen/underscore normalisation:

- `MUNITOAI_FREE_API_KEY` -> `munitoai_free_api_key` -> stem `munitoai_free` (underscore)
- `munitoai-free` (hyphen, the name documented at `proxy/config.yaml:254`) therefore never matches.

So the key had to be added under `munitoai_free`, not `munitoai-free`.

## Fix applied (operator-authorised)

- `~/.pi/agent/auth.json`: added `munitoai_free` = `{type: api_key, key: <copy of munitoai.key>}` (mode 600 preserved; backup at `auth.json.bak.20261016T233626`). The `munitoai-free` alias was also left in place.

## Intake interview — round 1 (OPEN QUESTIONs, awaiting producer answers)

**Evidence gathered so far (no questions needed, recorded for the brief):**
- `munitoai-free` (`proxy/config-fast.yaml` lines 48–61, 104–117, and the same entries in `proxy/config.yaml`) sits immediately after `local-qwen3` in the `plan`/`author`/`code` chains and has **no** `rate_limit_rpm`, so nothing gates it.
- The proxy already has a **proactive 60-second sliding-window RPM gate**: `SlidingWindowRateLimiter.check_and_increment()` (`proxy/proxy/rate_limiter.py`) invoked before dispatch in both fallback entry points (`provider.py:5900`, `provider.py:6840`). When the budget is exhausted it logs `Rate limited: skipping provider=…`, records `status=rate_limited`, and `continue`s to the next provider — i.e. **immediate pass-through, no waiting**. `rate_limit_rpm` is undocumented in any shipped config and is used by no provider today.
- `SlidingWindowRateLimiter.remaining()` exists but is never called — no capacity visibility in `/status`.
- Observed on 2026-10-18: up to 6 concurrent `MunitoAI Free` streams; `HTTP 429 rate_limit_exceeded` fallbacks; `fallback_after_queue` reasons. Upstream retries (`upstream_retry_max_attempts: 3`) do not re-consume budget.
- Neighbour items: `LP-0MVDNP36J006430L` (open, header-driven reset/cooldown — reactive), `LP-0MVCX0E2V001VB5N` (completed, per-account 429 must not exclude the paid sibling).

**Q1 (OPEN QUESTION) — what does the free tier's 60 s limit actually bound?** (a) request-rate budget, N requests per 60 s window; (b) concurrency, at most N in-flight streams; (c) per-request duration capped at 60 s upstream. *Agent preference: (a)* — matches the existing 60 s sliding-window gate and the observed burst pattern.

**Q2 (OPEN QUESTION) — how should the proxy learn the remaining capacity?** (a) static per-entry `rate_limit_rpm`; (b) derive from `x-ratelimit-remaining-requests` / `x-ratelimit-limit-requests` / `x-ratelimit-reset-requests` response headers (overlaps `LP-0MVDNP36J006430L`); (c) static cap now + header feedback later. *Agent preference: (c), with only the static cap in scope here.*

**Q3 (OPEN QUESTION) — acceptance bar for 'not over-using the free tier'?** (a) no upstream 429 from `munitoai-free` observed over a 24 h window; (b) every over-budget request logs `rate_limited` and proceeds to the next tier without waiting; (c) both. *Agent preference: (c).*

## Implementation notes (session herdr-1792321672-3518721-25934)

**Design.** Reused the existing proactive 60s sliding-window limiter rather than adding a scheduler:
- `proxy/proxy/provider_budget.py` (new) — `acquire_provider_budget()` decision + TTL-scoped session→entry affinity + bounded/depth-capped/abortable wait; reports `seconds_until_capacity()` from the limiter so the wait sleeps until the window drains instead of polling.
- `proxy/proxy/rate_limiter.py` — added `seconds_until_capacity()`; window pruning now uses `<=` so an entry exactly `window_seconds` old has left the window (a bounded waiter that sleeps to the window edge must find the slot free).
- `proxy/proxy/provider.py` — both fallback entry points (`_proxy_with_remote_fallback_cycle`, `_proxy_with_fallback`) now call the budget gate before dispatch; `_maybe_record_provider_affinity()` records affinity only on a 2xx dispatch; `format_budget_status()` exposes remaining/limit for the diagnostics table.
- `proxy/proxy/ui.py` — provider table shows `budget N/M per 60s` for gated entries.
- `proxy/config.yaml` + `proxy/config-fast.yaml` — `rate_limit_rpm: 10` on all six `munitoai-free` entries; new server keys `provider_rate_limit_wait_max_seconds: 60`, `provider_rate_limit_wait_max_waiters: 8`, `provider_affinity_ttl_seconds: 900`; documented in the config header + entry docs.
- Docs: `proxy/README.md`, `proxy/MODEL_ADD.md`, `proxy/docs/routing.md` (new budget table incl. the exhaustion-taxonomy `rate_limited` row).
- Fixtures/tests: golden merge fixtures + `BASE_ONLY_SERVER_KEYS` regenerated for the new inherited keys; `MUNITOAI_FREE_ENTRY` pin updated; new `proxy/tests/test_provider_budget.py` (19 tests: gate, new-session no-wait, bounded wait, wait cap, disconnect abort, waiter depth cap, TTL, affinity scoping, log/diagnostics, both fallback entry points, ungated regression).

**Assumption (documented):** `rate_limit_rpm: 10` is a starting value (observed peak was 41 dispatches per rolling minute, with 429s at peaks); tune from the `remaining=` field in the skip logs or via `LP-0MVDNP36J006430L` (header-derived budget).

**Known limitation:** the in-progress wait is silent (no SSE keep-alive comment) and is bounded at 60s by default; a follow-up could surface wait feedback to streaming clients the way chain-hold does.

## Preliminary results — run on demand, 2026-10-18 14:06 (post-change window ≈ 1.05 h)

**Verdict so far: working as designed — keep `rate_limit_rpm: 10` for now; confirm with the full 12 h window at the scheduled 02:05 run.**

**Window correction:** the gate went live earlier than the manual restart I mentioned earlier — commit `b71d743a` landed on `dev` at **12:39:25**, and the api-triggered restart at **13:05:09** loaded it. Post-change window therefore = 13:05:09 → 14:06:19 (1.02 h); baseline = the 12 h ending 13:05:09. Two further restarts fell inside the window (13:25:19 mode→fast, 13:59:38 manual), which reset the in-memory window and interrupted requests.

| Metric | Baseline (12 h) | Post-change (1.02 h) |
|---|---|---|
| `munito.ai` dispatches | 2 846 (3.95/min) | 303 (4.95/min) |
| Rolling-60 s max | **72** @ 01:08 | **11** @ 13:27 |
| Per-minute p50 / p95 / max | 4 / 20 / 44 | 5 / **10** / **10** |
| Minutes at/over the 10 cap | 96 (21.9 % of active min) | 11 (19.3 % of active min) |
| Minutes with any free-tier use | 439 (61.0 % of all min) | 57 (**93.2 %** of all min) |
| Upstream `429` markers | **19** (0.67 % of dispatches) | **0** |
| `All providers exhausted` | 1 | 0 |
| MunitoAI TTFT p50 / p95 | 0.560 s / 19.85 s | 0.587 s / **11.15 s** |

**AC1 — gate holds:** yes. Per-minute dispatch max is exactly 10 and never exceeds it; the single rolling-60 s reading of 11 is edge jitter (the limiter measures at decision time, the log timestamp is the POST a few ms later, so a decision just inside one window can land just outside it).

**AC2 — new sessions pass through with no wait:** 12 `Provider budget exhausted: … reason=rate_limited session_affinity=false` skips, **no wait of any kind** (there is no `session_affinity=false` entry in the wait log), each followed by dispatch on the next tier. Exhaustion diagnostics record them as `status=rate_limited` with `limit_rpm`/`remaining`/`reason`.

**AC3 — in-progress sessions wait, bounded:** 43 `wait start`, **43 satisfied, 0 exhausted, 0 aborted** — every wait produced a free-tier dispatch, none hit the 60 s cap and none lost a client. Wait distribution: p50 **14.1 s**, p95 **52.5 s**, max **55.4 s** (total 843 s across 43 requests, mean 19.6 s). No TTFT regression on the tier (p95 actually improved).

**AC4 — upstream 429s:** 19 in the baseline 12 h → **0** in the post-change hour. This is the failure mode the item was created for: agents were previously burning the allowance into `rate_limit_exceeded`.

**AC5 — free-tier utilisation preserved:** the tier is *not* starved — it is used in 93 % of minutes (vs 61 % baseline) at p50 5 dispatches/min, and saturates the cap in 19 % of active minutes (≈ baseline's 22 %). So the budget is absorbing the burst without idling the free tier.

**AC6 — recommendation:** keep `rate_limit_rpm: 10`; keep `provider_rate_limit_wait_max_seconds: 60` (p95 wait 52.5 s shows the cap is doing real work at the top end — do not raise it without evidence); keep `provider_affinity_ttl_seconds: 900`. Re-check at the scheduled run for: (a) whether the 19 % cap-saturation share rises (would push cost onto paid tiers), (b) whether waits stay under the cap under sustained load, (c) whether upstream 429s stay at zero.

**Caveats:** one hour of data, two in-window restarts, and a 60 s boundary jitter of ±1 dispatch. Figures above are a preliminary read; the one-shot scheduled run at 2026-10-19 02:05 re-measures the full 12 h window and will replace them.

data.author: Map
data.comment:
## Preliminary read — on-demand run 2026-10-18 17:35 (post-change window ≈ 4.2 h)

**Verdict (preliminary): the budget works as designed — the 10/min gate **holds** (measured == simulated cap-10 served exactly, both windows), upstream 429s dropped to ~0.3 % of dispatches, waits stay within the 15 s cap, and free-tier utilisation is preserved. The earlier sibling item LP-0MVDVJYN5001BMG4 already raised `rate_limit_rpm` 10 → 15 (commit `3a686659`, live at the **17:27 restart**); the measurement below is for the 10-era and the new 15-era is flagged separately.**

**CRITICAL note for the scheduled 02:05 run:** the live config is now `rate_limit_rpm: 15` (reserve 0.3, 15 s wait) since the 17:27 restart — NOT the 10 this item was designed to evaluate. The scheduled run must split its post-change window into the **10-era (13:05:09 → 17:27:00)** and the **15-era (17:27:00 → 02:05)**, or state explicitly which era it evaluates against which budget.

### Windows (log timestamps; rotation-agnostic parser over proxy.log + rotated siblings)
| window | span | hours | munito dispatches | upstream 429s (% of disp) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| base (pre-gate) | 10-18 01:05 → 13:05 | 12.0 | 2 846 | 11 (0.39 %) |
| v1 (rpm 10, wait 60 s) | 13:05:09 → 14:23:12 | 1.3 | 414 | 0 |
| v2 (rpm 10, reserve .3, wait 15 s) | 14:23:12 → 17:27 | 3.1 | 1 513 | 4 (0.26 %) |
| v3 (rpm 15, reserve .3, wait 15 s) | 17:27 → 17:31 | 0.07 | 128 (32/min) | 2 |

### AC1 — gate holds (rolling-60 s cap 10)
- Committed calibration (`proxy/benchmarks/munitoai_budget_eval.py`, limiter's own `<=`-pruned sliding window): **measured served == simulated cap-10 served exactly — v1: 414 = 414; v2: 1 513 = 1 513.** The limiter enforces 10 dispatches/rolling-60 s.
- Calendar-minute bucket max 20 (15:24) / rolling readings up to 23 at 17:24:18 are **not** cap violations: the limiter measures at decision time while the log timestamp is the POST a few ms later (rolling-window straddle), and **in-flight retries of the same logical request re-log "Stream started" without a new budget slot** (e.g. 17:24 minute: 15 POST lines from only 7 distinct `x-client-request-id`s). Dispatch-rate distribution (free, by minute): p50 **10**, p95 **10**, max 20 — i.e. the gate holds at exactly the cap.

### AC2 — new-session skips never wait
- v2 skips: **946** `Provider budget exhausted: skipping … session_affinity=false`, **0** with `session_affinity=true`.
- Wait-start events with `session_affinity=false`: **0** (of 930). Confirmed at the code level — the wait path is only entered for sessions with recorded affinity (`provider.py` → `acquire_provider_budget`).

### AC3 — in-progress waits, bounded ≤ 15 s
- v2: 930 wait start, **603 satisfied / 324 exhausted / 1 aborted / 0 declined**.
- Wait durations (satisfied+exhausted+aborted, n=928): p50 **7.9 s**, p95 **15.0 s**, max **15.0 s**, **0 > 15 s** ✓ (exhausted waits sit at exactly the 15 s cap, as designed).
- No TTFT regression on the tier (see latency below).

### AC4 — upstream 429s massively reduced
- 11 → 0 → 4: base 0.39 % of munito dispatches → v1 0 % → v2 0.26 % (4 in 3.1 h). Failure mode the item was created for (agents burning the allowance into `rate_limit_exceeded`) is eliminated.
- 429 onset knee (pre-gate): rolling-60 s dispatch rate at a 429 was min 8 / median 27 / max 63; per-minute 429 rate climbs from ~4 % (10–14/min) to 19.8 % (20–29/min) — the knee is ≈ 20/min, which is what justified raising to 15 (low-risk band).

### AC5 — free-tier utilisation preserved
- v1: used in 92.3 % of minutes, p50 5 disp/min. v2: used in **100 %** of minutes, p50 9 disp/min, 8.2 disp/active-min — not starved, but **v2 demand (rolling arrivals) p50 14 / p95 32 / max 47, share of minutes > 10 = 67.9 %** → at peak the cap is saturated and ~45 % of arrivals spill (93 % of spills → `opencode-go-3`; measured paid share 46 % at peak). The tier is right-sized at 10 for calm periods and under-provisioned at afternoon peaks (arithmetically unavoidable spill).

### AC6 — regression check
- `All providers exhausted`: base 1 → v1 0 → v2 0. No terminal 503 rise.
- MunitoAI TTFT: base p90 13.7 / p95 28.0 / p99 72.9 → v2 9.6 / 21.1 / 55.2 (no rise; waits are bounded so latency did not degrade).

### Recommendation (preliminary)
- **`rate_limit_rpm: 10` was effective for its purpose** (gate holds, 429s ~eliminated, waits ≤ 15 s, free tier utilised). It is **under-provisioned at afternoon demand peaks** (demand p50 14/min ≫ 10) → that spill is a config trade-off, not a failure.
- Raising to **15** (already applied by LP-0MVDVJYN5001BMG4, live 17:27) sits below the ≈20/min 429 knee and cuts peak spill ~40 % (45 % → 28 %); early 15-era data shows demand 32/min with 2 upstream 429s in the first 4 min — consistent with "sporadic, not sustained"; the rollback trigger in LP-0MVE0LUXN004PCO0 covers regression.
- **Keep** `provider_rate_limit_wait_max_seconds: 15` (cap verified to hold, 0 waits > 15 s; the 60 s era's p95 waits were the earlier latency problem) and **keep** `provider_affinity_ttl_seconds: 900`.
- Longer term the static value should give way to header-derived budgeting (`LP-0MVDNP36J006430L`) once the 15-era has a full window.
- No config/code change performed in this read-only session (per constraints).

### Caveats
- v2 spans 3.1 h only; in-window restarts at 13:25/13:59 (pre-v2). Scheduled 02:05 run replaces these with the full 12 h window; reproduce with the committed script:
  `python3 proxy/benchmarks/munitoai_budget_eval.py --end "2026-10-18 17:27:00"` for the 10-era, a separate run with `--gate-start "2026-10-18 17:27:00"` for the 15-era.
- Raw output (JSON) saved at `/tmp/budget-eval-prelim/report.json` for this run.

## Scheduled evaluation complete — keep `rate_limit_rpm: 15` (no change needed)

Ran at the scheduled 02:05 dispatch (executed 2026-10-19 03:25 local) per the
evaluation method, read-only over `/var/log/llama-proxy/proxy.log*`. Raw output:
`.worklog/analysis/LP-0MVDU4FDE003RQHS-budget-effectiveness.md` (reproducible
extractors + committed `proxy/benchmarks/munitoai_budget_eval.py`).

**Window note (config changed mid-window, as the 17:35 comment predicted):** the
post-change window 13:59:31 → 03:26 splits into **v1** (13:05:09→14:23:12,
rpm 10, no reserve, 60 s wait), **v2** (14:23:12→17:24:25, rpm 10, reserve 0.3,
15 s wait) and **v3** (17:24:25→03:26, rpm 15, = the raise by LP-0MVDVJYN5001BMG4;
boundary log-verified: last `limit=10` event 17:23:52, first `limit=15`
17:24:29). Baseline = 12 h preceding (01:59:31→13:59:31) plus a cleaner
pre-gate `base_clean` 01:59:31→13:05:09.

**AC1 — gate holds.** Distinct logical requests (`x-client-request-id`) per
minute: v1 max **9** ≤ 10, v2 max **8** ≤ 10, v3 max **8** ≤ 15; **0 minutes
over budget** in any era. Raw POST lines per minute sit exactly at the cap
(v1/v2 p50=10, v3 p50=15); raw max > cap (20 at 15:24, 17 rolling in v3) is
in-flight retries of the same logical request re-logging without a new budget
slot (15:24 minute: 20 lines / 7 request-ids) + ms decision/log straddle, not
over-dispatch. Limiter-semantics simulation (v2, 2 743 attempts): cap-10 model
serves 1 461 = measured 1 482 minus 21 retried re-logs; simulated spill 46.7 %
= measured 46.0 %.

**AC2 — new-session skips never wait.** 1 156 skips total (v1 24 / v2 941 /
v3 191), **all `session_affinity=false`**; 0 of 1 301 wait-starts carry
`session_affinity=false`. Every skip was followed by next-tier dispatch
(`fallback from=munitoai-free` counts match; `to=opencode-go-3` dominant).

**AC3 — waits bounded.** v2 (15 s cap): 921 start / 600 satisfied / 319
exhausted / 1 aborted; p50 7.75 s, **p95 15.0 s, max 15.0 s, 0 > 15 s**.
v3: 306/231/73/2; p50 5.01 s, **0 > 15 s**. v1 (60 s cap) p95 47.5 s — the
latency problem that justified the 15 s cap.

**AC4 — upstream 429s.** 6 in baseline (0.24 % of WB dispatches; base_clean
0.27 %) → **v1 0, v2 2 (0.135 %)** → the 10-budget cut the 429 share ~60 %
(v1+v2: 2/1 894 = 0.11 %) and near-zero absolute. **v3 (rpm 15) shows 429s
creeping back: 14/10 h (0.41 %)** — still half the pre-gate per-dispatch rate
(0.79 % over the committed script's 22 h window) but 3× the 10-era. **429
onset at 15: rolling rate at each v3 429 is median ≈ 13, range 6–15/min** —
the upstream's sustainable free-tier allowance sits at ~13–15/min, right at
our cap (pre-gate knee ≈ 20/min).

**AC5 — utilisation preserved.** Free tier used in 92–100 % of minutes post-gate
(vs 58–60 % pre-gate); 5.7–8.2 dispatches/active-min. But v2 demand p50
14/min, max 47/min → **46 % spill at cap 10**; cap 15 what-if on same stream
28.6 %, measured v3 **7.2 %** — the raise cut paid-tier pressure sharply.

**AC6 — regression.** `All providers exhausted` 1 pre-gate / 0 v1 / 0 v2 /
1 v3 (transient empty-unavailable, not a 429 exclusion) — no increase. TTFT:
v2 p95 21.2 s vs baseline 16.2 s (the 15 s wait cap doing real work at the
saturated afternoon peak), p99 *better* (55.2 vs 63.3 s); v3 p50/p90/p95 all
below baseline — no wait-caused latency regression.

## Recommendation: KEEP `rate_limit_rpm: 15` (current live value — no config/code change)

- The **10-budget was effective for its purpose** (gate holds, 429s ~60 %
  down to 0.11 %, waits ≤ 15 s, tier used 100 % of minutes) but
  **under-provisioned at afternoon demand peaks** (46 % spill).
- The already-applied **raise to 15 is justified by demand evidence** (holds
  the gate, spill 46 % → 7.2 % measured, 429 share still half pre-gate) —
  therefore **do not revert to 10**.
- **Do not raise above 15**: v3 429s onset at 6–15/min (median ≈ 13) — the
  cap sits at the upstream sustainable edge; 20 re-enters the pre-gate 429
  knee (19.8 % of minutes at 20–29/min had a 429).
- **Keep** `provider_rate_limit_reserve_ratio: 0.3`,
  `provider_rate_limit_wait_max_seconds: 15` and
  `provider_affinity_ttl_seconds: 900` (all verified; 0 waits > 15 s).
- **Monitor the 15-era 429 signal** (14/10 h) via the existing rollback
  trigger LP-0MVE0LUXN004PCO0; the durable fix is header-derived budgeting
  (LP-0MVDNP36J006430L) once a full 15-era window exists — the static value
  sits at the exact upstream edge and an adaptive gate removes the guesswork.

No follow-up work item created: the recommendation requires no config or code
change (current live config already matches it); related successors
(LP-0MVDNP36J006430L, LP-0MVE0LUXN004PCO0) are already open.

Caveat: v2/v3 boundaries are log-verified (~17:24:25) and differ slightly from
the estimates in earlier comments (17:27:00); all figures above are from the
deduplicated on-line log timestamps (rotation is not trusted).

## Implementation notes

**Reserve (AC1/AC2).** `provider_budget.reserved_slots(rpm, config)` = `min(floor(rpm * provider_rate_limit_reserve_ratio), rpm - 1)`, 0 when `rpm <= 1` or the ratio is 0. `acquire_provider_budget()` now applies a per-request cap: in-progress sessions (affinity) use the full `rate_limit_rpm`; new/anonymous sessions use `new_session_limit()` = `rpm - reserve` (7 of 10 with the shipped values). The limiter's single sliding window plus these per-caller caps make the reserve exact and race-free.

**Wait cap (AC3).** `_DEFAULT_WAIT_MAX_SECONDS` 60 → **15**; `provider_rate_limit_wait_max_seconds: 15` in `config.yaml`. An in-progress session that still cannot get a slot after 15 s passes through (`rate_limited_after_wait`).

**Observability (AC5).** `BudgetDecision` gains `reserve_slots`/`effective_limit`; both fallback entry points record them in the attempt diagnostics and the skip log now reads `... limit=7 reserve=3 remaining=3 reason=rate_limited session_affinity=false`.

**Tests.** 7 new cases in `test_provider_budget.py` (reserve boundary new vs in-progress, ratio 0 = previous behaviour, rpm=1 and ratio 1.0 clamping, 15 s default cap, wait-wins-inside-cap, no new-session waiting, log/diagnostics fields, end-to-end 8th-session→paid-tier) plus the legacy `test_rate_limiter.py` integration expectation updated for the reserve (4 of 5 slots for an anonymous session, 1 reserved) with the reason inline.

**Config/docs/fixtures.** `provider_rate_limit_reserve_ratio: 0.3` added (inherited-only key, so golden merge fixtures + `BASE_ONLY_SERVER_KEYS` updated); `proxy/README.md`, `proxy/docs/routing.md` (behaviour table + 'why the reserve exists' with the measured latency numbers) and `proxy/MODEL_ADD.md` updated.

## Measurement table — should `munitoai-free` rate_limit_rpm be raised? (AC1–AC4)

**Reproducible analysis:** `proxy/benchmarks/munitoai_budget_eval.py` (committed with this
item). Runs, e.g.:
`python3 proxy/benchmarks/munitoai_budget_eval.py --end "2026-10-18 16:52:00" --out <dir>`.
All data from `/var/log/llama-proxy/proxy.log*` (per-line timestamps; rotation-agnostic),
filtered strictly to the windows below.

### Windows
| window | span | hours | free dispatches | arrivals* | upstream 429s |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| base (pre-gate) | 10-17 15:05 → 10-18 13:05 | 22.0 | 8936 | 8936 | 71 (0.79 %) |
| v1 (gate 10, wait 60 s) | 13:05:09 → 14:23:12 | 1.3 | 414 | 439 | 0 |
| v2 (gate 10 + reserve 0.3, wait 15 s) | 14:23:12 → 16:52 | 2.5 | 1199 | 2185 | 2 (0.17 %) |

\* arrivals = dispatches + `Provider budget exhausted` skips + wait-exhausted/aborted/declined
(new + affinity demand for the entry). Gate went live at the **13:05:09 restart**, the
reserve+15 s cap at the **14:23:12 restart** (log markers; note LP-0MVDU4FDE's 13:59:31
restart predates the first budget lines by ~1 h).

### AC1 — demand (rolling-60 s arrivals per minute)
| window | p50 | p95 | p99 | max | share of minutes > 10 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| base | 3 | 25 | 39.8 | 61 | 23.7 % |
| v1 | 5 | 11.1 | 13.4 | 15 | 11.4 % |
| v2 | 13 | 32 | 39.0 | 47 | **63.8 %** |

Demand regularly exceeds 10/min (v2 = afternoon peak): spill is arithmetically unavoidable
at 10 during such windows.

### AC1 — what-if spill at candidate budgets (sliding-60 s, limiter's own semantics)
| budget | v2 served | v2 spilled | **v2 spill share** | base spill share (22 h) | v1 spill share |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 10 simulated | 1209 | 976 | 44.7 % | 41.4 % | 5.7 % |
| 10 **measured** (shipped config) | 1199 | 986 | 45.1 % | — | 5.7 % |
| 12 | 1385 | 800 | 36.6 % | 34.7 % | 2.3 % |
| **15** | 1596 | 589 | **27.0 %** | 26.7 % | 0.5 % |
| 20 | 1826 | 359 | 16.4 % | 17.1 % | 0.0 % |

The simulation reproduces the measured spill at N=10 almost exactly (44.7 % vs 45.1 %),
so the higher-budget rows are calibrated.

### AC2 — upstream 429 onset (the knee)
- Pre-gate: rolling-60 s dispatch rate at a 429 was min **8**, median **28**, max **63**.
- Pre-gate 429-minute rate by rolling-60 s dispatch bin: 0–4 → **0.5 %**; 5–9 → 3.0 %;
  10–14 → 4.0 %; 15–19 → 5.6 %; **20–29 → 19.8 %**; 30–39 → 47.1 %; 40–59 → 100 %; 60+ → 100 %.
- **The knee is ≈ 20 dispatches/rolling-60 s.** 10–15/min is a low-risk band (~4–6 % of
  minutes); ≥ 20/min climbs steeply.
- Post-gate at cap 10: **2** 429s in 2.5 h (v2), both when the rolling count hit exactly 10
  with dense sub-minute bursts (10–13 dispatches in ~60–70 s). Note: the item context
  ("0 upstream 429s since the gate") predates the 14:48:18 429 and is inaccurate.

### AC3 — paid-spill cost per candidate (v2 peak window)
Measured at 10: remote share = **1199 api.munito.ai vs 1025 opencode.ai (46.1 % paid)**; the
rate-limit fallback to `opencode-go-3` was 980 of 986 spills. Projected paid share with the
same arrival stream:
- **12** → ≈ 37.7 % paid; **15** → ≈ **28 %** paid; **20** → ≈ 18 % paid.
(base regression control: paid share was 5.3 % in the 22 h pre-gate period — the gate's
trade-off is paid-spill vs no 429s.)

### AC4 — latency (no regression)
- **Waits (v2):** n=709, p50 8.0 s, p90 = p95 = p99 = **15.0 s**, max **15.0 s**, **0 waits > 15 s** ✓.
- **Free-tier first-token (ttft_seconds):** base p90 13.7 / p95 28.0 / p99 72.9 → v2 11.4 / 22.9 / 55.8
  (no rise; v2 better than the pre-gate baseline).

### Recommendation (AC4)
**Raise `rate_limit_rpm` 10 → 15** (applied in this item — AC5), because the knee is ≈ 20/min and
15 sits in the low-429 band (pre-gate 15–19/min: 5.6 % of minutes) while cutting the paid spill
by ~40 % vs 10 (45 % → 27 %; opencode share 46 % → ≈ 28 %). Expected effect:
- **429s:** per dispatch rises from ~0.2 % (at 10) toward, at most, the ~4–6 %-of-minutes band
  observed pre-gate at 14–19/min — sporadic, **not sustained**; with the reserve/wait gate's
  smoothing, actual is expected below that.
- **Paid spill:** ~−40 % of rate-limit fallbacks at peak (≈ 400 fewer opencode dispatches per
  2.5 h peak window).
- **Latency:** unchanged (waits ≤ 15 s cap holds; TTFT no regression).
- **Rollback trigger:** 24 h observation check-in (follow-up item **LP-0MVE0LUXN004PCO0**) reverts
  to 10 if the upstream-429 *minute* rate at peak exceeds ~10 % or a sustained burst occurs.

### AC5/AC6 — adopted change
- `rate_limit_rpm: 15` applied to the `plan`/`author`/`code` `munitoai-free` entries in
  `proxy/config.yaml` **and** `proxy/config-fast.yaml` (reserve 0.3 unchanged → new-session
  cap 11, affinity cap 15); golden merge fixtures, `test_munitoai_fallback_chain.py`, and docs
  (`proxy/README.md`, `proxy/docs/routing.md`, `proxy/MODEL_ADD.md`) updated; full test suite
  green via the test skill.
- **Observation window:** T0 = the next proxy restart (the config needs a restart to take
  effect; not performed here to avoid dropping live sessions — restart via
  `/skill:start-proxy --restart`). Follow-up check-in LP-0MVE0LUXN004PCO0 is scheduled

data.comment:
### Answering 'is the rate limit used for any other provider?' (fact-finding for this item)

Resolved config across both modes — `rate_limit_rpm` is declared on **exactly one logical entry**:

| Entry | Type | Endpoint | `rate_limit_rpm` |
|---|---|---|---|
| `munitoai-free` (plan/author/code) | remote | api.munito.ai | **10** |
| `munitoai` (paid) | remote | api.munito.ai | — |
| `opencode-go-3` / `-2` / `-go` | remote | opencode.ai/zen/go | — |
| `opencode-go-compact` | remote | opencode.ai/zen/go | — |
| `deepseek-flash` / `-compact` | remote | api.deepseek.com | — |
| `github-primary` | remote | models.inference.ai.azure.com | — |
| `local-qwen3` / `local-embed` | local | — | — |

So the capability is **dormant for every other provider** (it was already before the free-tier work: no shipped config ever set it). Any paid tier could opt in later — e.g. to protect a per-key concurrency/rate ceiling on `opencode` or a paid MunitoAI plan — which is exactly why per-model + per-entry controls matter: today the *behaviour* knobs (reserve ratio, wait cap, waiter depth, affinity TTL) are global, so opting a second provider in would force all chains to share one tuning.

Note for implementers: the budget bucket is keyed by provider **entry name**, so `plan`/`author`/`code` share one 10/min window. Per-model knobs change *how* a model behaves against that shared window, not the size of the window.

### Implementation notes — model/entry `budget` blocks (option (a) as specified)

No OPEN QUESTION was widened here: gating the `models.compact` summarizer dispatch remains `LP-0MVFYYYXS0011T58` (still blocked) and this item does not touch `compaction_summarizer.py`.

**What landed**
- `provider_budget.resolve_budget_settings(provider_cfg, config, model_config)` resolves each of `reserve_ratio`, `wait_max_seconds`, `max_waiters`, `affinity_ttl_seconds` per knob through **entry `budget` > `models.<name>.budget` > `server.*` > built-in default**, returning `BudgetSettings` plus a `sources` map (`entry`/`model`/`server`/`default`).
- `BudgetDecision.sources` / `.source_label` expose provenance as `knob@layer` (e.g. `reserve_ratio@model`). Log lines and the diagnostics attempt entry append `budget_source=…` **only** when a model/entry block supplied a value, which is what keeps AC3 byte-identical for the shipped config.
- `acquire_provider_budget()` gained a `model_config=` keyword; both fallback entry points pass their request's model config (AC7), and both record a `budget_source` field on `rate_limited` / `rate_limited_waited` attempts (AC6).
- `_maybe_record_provider_affinity(..., model_config=...)` records affinity with the **model-resolved** TTL, so the recorded lifetime matches the chain that created it (AC1 `affinity_ttl_seconds`). Lookup needed no change: the stored expiry is already absolute.
- Existing single-knob helpers (`wait_max_seconds`, `wait_max_waiters`, `reserve_ratio`, `affinity_ttl_seconds`, `reserved_slots`, `new_session_limit`) keep their signatures and now delegate to the resolver, so every existing caller/test is unchanged.

**Assumptions documented**
1. **AC4 (out-of-range vs malformed).** The Desired-change text says values are "clamped/validated exactly as the server-level knobs are today (ratio to [0,1], wait/TTL to >= 0, malformed values fall back to the default with a warning)", while AC4 says out-of-range values "fall back to the next layer". Implemented as: **unparseable values fall through to the next layer with a warning; out-of-range values are clamped into range with a warning** — i.e. today's clamping semantics are preserved at every layer and only malformed input falls through. Both cases are logged, neither raises nor blocks a request, and tests cover both per key. This keeps "clamped exactly as the server-level knobs are today" true.
2. **Log byte-identity (AC3)** is achieved by emitting the provenance suffix only when a model/entry block contributed; server/default-only configs (including the shipped `config.yaml`) produce the exact previous format — pinned by a test that asserts the full skip line verbatim.
3. **No model *quota*** was introduced: the limiter bucket stays keyed by provider entry, proven by a test where two models with different `budget` blocks exhaust one shared `rate_limit_rpm` window.

**Tests** (`proxy/tests/test_provider_budget.py`, new section): precedence matrix for all four knobs × six layer combinations (AC2), one behaviour test per knob (AC1), entry-over-model override, byte-identical decision + log line with no blocks (AC3), malformed + out-of-range per knob and a fully-garbage block (AC4), shared-window proof (AC5), skip-log + diagnostics provenance and the empty-provenance case (AC6), and a spy test proving both `_proxy_with_remote_fallback_cycle` and `_proxy_with_fallback_cycle` hand the model config to the gate (AC7). `proxy/tests/test_provider_context_limit.py` had one budget spy updated for the new keyword-only-in-practice parameter.

**Verification**: full pytest suite green (`run_tests.py --scope full`), ruff clean on the changed files.

## 24 h check-in report — munitoai-free rate_limit_rpm: 15 (LP-0MVE0LUXN004PCO0)

**Reproducible analysis:** `python3 proxy/benchmarks/munitoai_budget_eval.py --gate-start "2026-10-18 18:06:29" --reserve-start "2026-10-18 18:06:29" --end "2026-10-19 10:19:20" --out <dir>`; all numbers below reproduce from `/var/log/llama-proxy/proxy.log*` (rotation-agnostic per-line timestamps).

### 0. Restart-marker verification (T0) — ⚠️ env var points at the wrong restart

- `$MUNITOAI_CHECKIN_CHANGE_TS = 2026-10-19 18:46:02` is the **latest** restart, but that restart loads **`rate_limit_rpm: 2`** (LP-0MVF19DKR008VCHO, commit 24348bfa 10:15:39 +0100; `limit=2` budget lines start 10:19:26). Using it as T0 would measure the wrong (stale) config — rejected.
- The **first restart carrying 15** after the 10→15 push (3a686659, pushed 16:29 UTC 10-18) is **2026-10-18 18:06:29** (local) — confirmed via budget log lines: first `limit=15` / `limit=11 reserve=4` lines at 07:11–07:12 on 10-19 (no budget-pressure lines overnight because demand stayed under the cap, not because the config was old).
- **The 15 experiment was truncated**: the restart at **2026-10-19 10:19:20** loads `rate_limit_rpm: 2` (approved LP-0MVF19DKR008VCHO), i.e. the observation at 15 is **[T0, 2026-10-19 10:19:20) = 16.2 h**, not the full 24 h. The remainder of the 24 h ran at cap 2 and is **not** attributable to the 15 experiment. Re-scheduling produces no additional limit-15 data (config is now 2), so this check-in closes with the decisive truncated window noted below.

### 1. Window summary
| window | span | hours | free dispatches | arrivals | upstream 429s |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| base (pre-change, 22 h) | 10-17 20:06:29 → 10-18 18:06:29 | 22.0 | 9288 | 10731 | 64 (0.69 % of disp) |
| **v2 = at 15 (T0→truncation)** | 10-18 18:06:29 → 10-19 10:19:20 | **16.2** | 4697 | 4977 | **6 (0.128 % of disp)** |
| (reference v2 at 10) | 10-18 14:23:12 → 16:52 | 2.5 | 1199 | 2185 | 2 (0.17 %) |

### AC1 — upstream-429 rate at 15 (rollback-trigger check)
- **Absolute:** 6 in 16.2 h (0.37/h); **all** were `rate_limit_exceeded` at `https://api.munito.ai/inference`.
- **Per hour:** 10-18 22:00→1, 23:00→4, 10-19 00:00→1; all other hours 0. Per-hour histogram in the item's constraint of "429 minute rate at peak".
- **Share of munitoai dispatches:** 6/4697 = **0.128 %** (vs 0.17 % at cap 10, 0.69 % pre-gate) — no rise.
- **Peak-demand criterion (≥ 20 free arrivals in rolling-60 s):** only **7 minutes** in the window qualified (p50 28, max 51 arrivals/min); **0/7 had an upstream 429 = 0 %** — far below the ~10 % trigger.
- **Minutes-by-band (arrivals, 429-minute rate):** 0–4: 0.2 %; 5–9: 0.9 %; 10–14: 1.6 %; 15–19: 1.7 %; **20–29 / 30–39 / 40–59: 0 % each** (no 429 ever occurred at ≥ 20/min). Dispatch-based bands agree.
- **Burst clause (borderline, NOT attributable):** 4 429s in 8 minutes at 23:20–23:27 on 10-18 (two 2-minute runs) — a multi-minute episode; **however** all occurred at **9–14 dispatches/rolling-60 s — at/below the 15 cap and far below the ≈20/min knee**, and an equal/larger burst existed at cap 10 before the change (8 429s in 25 min at 17:25–17:50 on 10-18 at 8–15/min). The 15 window's per-dispatch 429 rate (0.128 %) is **lower** than at cap 10 → the raise did not push the free tier into upstream rejection.
- **Pass/fail: PASS on the quantitative rule; burst clause marginal but not change-attributable.** Rollback trigger **not triggered**.

### AC2 — spill & paid share at 15 (vs LP-0MVDVJYN5001BMG4 predictions)
| metric | predicted at 15 | **measured at 15 (this window)** | at 10 (same window sim) |
|---|---|---|---|
| spill share | ≈27 % | 280/4977 = **5.6 %** (sim at cap 15: 4.9 %) | sim 19.2 % |
| opencode paid share of remote | ≈28 % | 169/4866 = **3.5 %** | 46 % baseline |

Measured spill is **below** the prediction because window demand was lower than the 2.5 h peak used for prediction (demand p95 15/min vs 32/min; p99 19 vs 39). The raise to 15 cut simulated spill ~74 % vs the same window at 10 (19.2 % → 4.9 %) and the paid share fell to ~3.5 % — the predicted paid-spill reduction materialised.

### AC3 — latency (no regression)
- **Waits:** n=465, p50 3.95 s, p90 14.97 s, p95 = p99 = 15.0 s, max 15.0 s, **0 waits > 15 s** ✓ (32 sat at the 15 s cap; 91 wait-exhausted).
- **Free-tier first-token (ttft_seconds):** count 4664, p50 0.69 s, p90 **9.61** s, p95 **16.49** s, p99 **39.95** s vs baseline p90 12.16 / p95 23.8 / p99 65.27 — **no rise; improved**.

### AC4 — Verdict: **KEEP 15** (no rollback); superseded in practice by the later cut to 2
- Evidence: 429-minute rate at peak demand = 0 % (trigger ~10 %); per-dispatch 429 rate 0.128 % ≤ at-10 baseline; spill 5.6 % (predicted ≈27 %, better due to quieter window) with paid share 3.5 %; waits ≤ 15 s and TTFT no rise.

Reverting "to 10" here would *raise* the limit against the operator's newer decision — neither required by the trigger nor appropriate.
- AC5 (revert/adjust implementation) **not applicable** — no code change performed, so no test run per the check-in constraints.

### Caveat
The 15-window is 16.2 h, not 24 h, because the approved cut to 2 truncated it. Within that window the rollback trigger was not met; results are decisive for the question "does 15 drive sustained 429s / does spill-reduction materialise" — answer: no / yes.

data.comment:
Implementation complete, pushed to dev in commit 0281c93f (branch wl-LP-0MVECX47Z004LJAQ-adopted-llama-server-loses-its-log-sink).

## Root cause confirmed
spawn_and_capture() started llama-server with stdout=subprocess.PIPE plus a proxy-owned reader thread. On a proxy-only restart the new proxy ADOPTS the running backend but the reader thread died with the old proxy, leaving the pipe with writers only - llama-server.log froze indefinitely.

## Changes
1. AC1/AC5 - relay owned by the backend. spawn_and_capture() now redirects llama-server stdout/stderr DIRECTLY into llama-server.log (real file object passed as the child stdout). The write fd is held by the backend, so a proxy-only restart that adopts the backend keeps the log flowing with no re-attachment and no forced backend restart (warm prompt cache preserved). The legacy pipe relay is retained only when no real log file exists (DEVNULL/None).
2. AC2 - loud, never silent. _verify_adopted_log_relay() runs on every adoption: if the log exists but no process holds it open for writing (pre-fix pipe-based backend), it logs a WARNING and sets llama_log_source_unhealthy. It deliberately does NOT restart (AC5).
3. AC3 - observable freshness. GET /health now reports llama_log_age_seconds and llama_log_source_healthy. Write-only fd detection uses /proc/<pid>/fdinfo access-mode flags (read-only viewers/tailers are ignored) and excludes the proxy's own log handle.
4. Progress logging preserved. Extracted _ProgressLogger; prefill progress lines are now recovered by a llama-server.log tailer that follows rotation and is (re)started on adoption - so re-attachment is literal. start_llama_server() clears a stale unhealthy flag.
5. Tests: proxy/tests/test_log_relay_adoption.py (18 hermetic tests). Docs: proxy/README.md llama-server log section documents the durable relay and the new /health fields.

## Verification
- Full suite green at the pushed commit (run_tests.py --scope full): 0 failures.
- Ruff clean; refactor pipeline: 0 smells.

data.author: Map
data.comment:
Implementation notes (LP-0MVF0N9SA0071LWM)

Root cause confirmed: the budget skip in `acquire_provider_budget` records no cooldown and no usage-limit quarantine, so the generic exhaustion payload has `unavailable={}`. `_compute_retry_after` then has no candidate and returns 0, so `_bounded_hold_seconds` returned 0.0 (the LP-0MU56ZKQD005SX08 instant-retry branch) and `_run_chain_cycles` replayed all 3 cycles inside the still-full window.

Change (proxy/proxy/provider.py):
- New `_budget_window_retry_after(diagnostics)`: for every diagnostics entry that is a budget skip (`status == "rate_limited"`, i.e. the only status the budget gate records), ask the rate limiter `seconds_until_capacity(entry, effective_limit, 60)` and take the EARLIEST positive rollover (the chain succeeds as soon as ANY gated entry regains capacity). Returns 0 when no budget-skipped entry is waiting on its window, so genuine instant recovery is untouched.
- `_build_exhausted_response` uses the derived value ONLY when the cooldown/reset computation yields 0, so genuine instant recovery is untouched (AC2). The value flows into both the JSON `retry_after` and the `Retry-After` header (AC4), so `_bounded_hold_seconds` now returns a positive hold instead of 0.0 (AC1).

Assumptions / decisions (documented here and in the docs):
- The derived wait is inherently <= the 60 s limiter window, so it fit within the configured chain-hold budgets (chain_hold_seconds 300 / chain_hold_total_seconds 720) without an extra cap; `_bounded_hold_seconds` still caps a hold at `chain_hold_seconds` and returns immediately when the rollover cannot fit the total hold budget (doomed-hold guard preserved, AC3).
- `provider_rate_limit_wait_max_seconds` (15 s, in-progress dispatch wait) was intentionally NOT used as the cap: the chain-hold budget is the governing bound for a held request, and clamping to 15 s would end the hold before a 60 s window could roll over, reproducing the failure. Documented in proxy/config.yaml and proxy/docs/remote-fallback-timeout-budget.md.
- The advertised value is still capped by `max_retry_after_seconds` (client-facing cap).

Tests: proxy/tests/test_chain_hold_budget_window.py (11 tests) — measured 13/11 regression (positive hold, next cycle succeeds once the window frees), AC2 zero-latency preservation, AC3 total budget, AC4 header/body parity, streaming feedback, precedence over cooldown-derived waits, and the earliest-freeing-provider selection.

## Appendix: planning questions & decisions

Recorded by the `plan` skill session `herdr-1792390902-3844878-15177`.

### Q1. Which opencode-go entry joins the low chain?
`proxy/config.yaml` defines three equivalent entries: `opencode-go-3` (OPENCODE_3_API_KEY), `opencode-go-2` (OPENCODE_2_API_KEY), `opencode-go` (OPENCODE_API_KEY), all with `deepseek-v4.1-flash` and identical `available_times`.
**Answer (eng, recommended, for confirmation):** `opencode-go-3` — it is first in the medium/high provider lists for the code model, so reusing it for the low chain keeps prompt-cache affinity aligned with the hot path. Evidence: `proxy/config.yaml` model `code` → `providers[2].name == opencode-go-3`.
**Status:** OPEN QUESTION (confirm at implementation).

### Q2. UTC vs local window alignment
`available_times` are **UTC**; the priority cheap window (`priority_window: 01:00–10:00`) is **local time**.
**Research:** host timezone is `Europe/Dublin` (IST, +0100 in October), so the cheap window is UTC **00:00–09:00**. opencode-go windows are UTC `["00:00-01:00", "04:00-06:00", "10:00-00:00"]`, i.e. unavailable UTC `01:00–04:00` and `06:00–10:00`. Overlap = UTC `00:00–01:00` + `04:00–06:00` = **3 of 9 cheap hours**. Evidence: `date -u` output and `proxy/config.yaml` `available_times` / `priority_window`.
**Answer (recommended):** keep `available_times` unchanged — "off-peak only" is the requirement, and the gaps are deliberate paid-spend avoidance. Document the 3-of-9 overlap in config comments so the limitation is explicit rather than surprising.
**Status:** decided for this item; the widening question is an OPEN QUESTION below.

### OPEN QUESTION (operator): widen the windows?
The change yields ~3 extra hours of local-overflow capacity per night, not 9. If more cheap-window coverage is wanted, opencode-go `available_times` would need to cover UTC `01:00–04:00` and `06:00–10:00` too — which means paid spend in the currently-excluded hours. This item deliberately does **not** do that. Directed to the operator; matters because it is the difference between a 3-hour and a 9-hour fix.

### Q3. Should the `compact` model's low chain change?
`compact` already chains `low: [opencode-go-compact, deepseek-flash-compact]` — it has no local tier and already leads with opencode-go.
**Answer (eng):** no. Out of scope; leave untouched.

### Duplicate-work check
`wl search "opencode-go"` / `"off-peak"` / `"low priority"` reviewed. Nearest neighbours: LP-0MSXPHTD9004DZ4P (added the off-peak `available_times` windows — prerequisite, completed), LP-0MVDT94F0003VHUA (introduced priority routing and the `low = local + free` chain — the constraint being relaxed here, completed), LP-0MSMIPPJI007GU9N (cheap mode keeps remote enabled — completed). **No duplicate found:** none adds opencode-go to a `low` chain.

## Operator decision recorded — plan revised

**Q1 resolved:** do **not** pick a single opencode entry — add **all** opencode models to the low chain, gated by their existing `available_times`.

**Q2 resolved:** do **not** widen `available_times`. The off-peak windows stay exactly as they are; paid spend remains confined to them. The measured 3-of-9-hour overlap is therefore accepted as the intended benefit, not a defect to fix.

Resulting target chain for plan/author/code:

`local-qwen3 → munitoai-free → opencode-go-3 → opencode-go-2 → opencode-go`

### Why "all three" is substantive, not cosmetic (new evidence)

Rate-limit quarantine is keyed on the **API-key account**, not the gateway:
`_usage_limit_account_key()` = `api_key_env@endpoint` (`proxy/proxy/provider.py:4075-4090`, LP-0MSMBWB23009XYPW / LP-0MVCX0E2V001VB5N). A 429 on `opencode-go-3` poisons only that account, so `opencode-go-2` and `opencode-go` are still tried in the same request with independent quota → genuine 3× rate-limit capacity. This is exactly the failure mode observed (16 upstream 429s from `api.munito.ai`, `rate_limited` 1540).

**Caveat recorded (added as an AC and a required doc point):** for 5xx/stall failures the same-gateway siblings ARE skipped as one failure domain (`_failure_domain_key` / `attempted_domains`, LP-0MSG45I8Q0020N1F), so the three entries do **not** multiply capacity during an opencode outage. Expected, but must be documented to avoid a false resilience assumption.

### Correction to the earlier problem statement

The parent description previously said `munitoai-free` was capped at `rate_limit_rpm: 15`. That figure came from the config's documentation comment; the **actual** per-model values are `rate_limit_rpm: 2` for plan/author/code. Corrected in the description — it makes the overflow problem materially worse than first stated (2 req/min, and it is the last entry in the chain).

```
02:00:03 Skipping provider=opencode-go-3: outside its available_times window (UTC)   <- other request, gate works
02:00:05 Skipping provider=opencode-go-2: outside its available_times window (UTC)
02:00:05 Skipping provider=opencode-go: quota_exhausted (account=OPENCODE_API_KEY, ...)
02:00:05 Fallback triggered ... from=munitoai-free, to=opencode-go-3, reason=rate_limited
02:00:05 Stream started: provider=OpenCode Go 3 ... entry=opencode-go-3
```

Notice `opencode-go-3`'s skip line is **absent** in that sequence although the same entry was skipped two seconds earlier — the gate is not disabled for `-3`, so this is a per-request eligibility/bypass path worth a look. Filed as **LP-0MVI9TXIZ0077PZV** (bug, discovered-from this item) rather than fixed here, since this item is measurement-only.

So the honest statement is: **no systemic leakage** (1 event, 0.1% of the window's 5,572 opencode fallbacks, 2 dispatches) but not literally zero. AC3 as written ("zero") is therefore unmet; the intent (paid spend confined to permissible times) holds to within 0.006% of tokens.

### AC4 — per-key dispatch counts: **more than one key used; no exclusion bug**

Post-change 24 h window, dispatches by `entry=`:

| Entry | API key | Dispatches | Skips observed |
|---|---|---|---|
| `opencode-go-3` | `OPENCODE_3_API_KEY` | **11,106** | outside window 924, cooldown 31, same-failure-domain 3 |
| `opencode-go-2` | `OPENCODE_2_API_KEY` | **30** (15 fallbacks) | outside window 925, cooldown 2, same-failure-domain 197 |
| `opencode-go` | `OPENCODE_API_KEY` | **0** | `quota_exhausted` 937, same-failure-domain 200 |

- Failover to a second account **does** engage (`-2` served 30 requests, 14 of them after a `munitoai-free` rate-limit). The low count reflects the small number of account-3 429s (36 `HTTP 429` fallback reasons; 60 upstream 429s from `opencode-go`), not an exclusion bug.
- The third key's **zero** is explained by quota state, not by exclusion: every visit logged `Skipping provider=opencode-go: quota_exhausted (account=OPENCODE_API_KEY, effective_headroom=0.0%, resets_in≈200,600 s)` (reset ≈2026-10-23).
- Over the 48 h secondary window all three keys did receive traffic — `-3` 18,995, `-2` 30, `opencode-go` 13,817 — which confirms the third key is reachable when it has headroom (see the surge note below).

### AC5 — cost statement: **no low-chain-driven rise in paid spend outside the overlap hours**

- **Inside** the permissible overlap windows: 137.2 M paid tokens (16.6% of the window's logged tokens) via 915 fallbacks / 1,806 dispatches — this is the change doing exactly what it was built to do.
- **Inside the forbidden gap windows**: 52.3 k paid tokens (0.006%), one event (see AC3). Baseline: 0.
- **Absolute paid volume rose** (421.7 M → 828.5 M logged tokens, +96%) while **requests fell** (12,810 → 9,137), i.e. tokens per request ≈2.8×. Of the logged tokens, 100% were served by paid entries in **both** windows (baseline `opencode-go-3` 99.98% + `-2` 0.02%; post `-3` 99.36% + `-2` 0.20% + `deepseek-flash` 0.44%), so the *paid share of logged tokens did not rise* — the denominator grew.
- That growth cannot be attributed to LP-0MVF1FQJR000NH2I: **seven other config/code changes landed inside the observation window** (`42f93580`, `f496626e` local admission/prefill; `c443240c`, `ec5514fc`, `242d03f4`, `6999492a`, `a8b56995`), and the proxy was restarted at 2026-10-20 13:10 local. Track the token-volume trend separately; it is not a regression of this change.
- **One documented exception to window discipline, not a regression:** in the 48 h window the `OPENCODE_API_KEY` account entered the final-week **quota-surge bypass** (`quota_surge_bypass entered provider=opencode-go account=OPENCODE_API_KEY resets_at=2026-10-23T08:43:55Z`, 2026-10-20 01:00 UTC; feature LP-0MVF7KJN2000ASE8, `quota_surge_enabled: true`, `quota_surge_days: 7`). That lift is purposeful use-it-or-lose-it spend at any hour and accounts for the 196 M gap-hour tokens / 3,255 dispatches in the 48 h window. It is independent of the 5-entry low chain.

### AC6 — sample-size caveat and the counts the verdict rests on

- Low-priority sample: **2,202** request-level `priority_decision priority=low` in the 24 h window (23.5% of 9,380 decisions; of these 2,037 had no `X-Priority` header, 165 carried a spoofed `high` that was correctly capped, 2 were explicit `low`). Baseline: 2,257. The request-level sample is **comparable**, not thin.
- The verdict nevertheless rests on modest absolute numbers and I state them: **915** overlap-window opencode fallbacks (AC2), **1** gap-window fallback / 2 dispatches / 52.3 k tokens (AC3), **30 / 0** dispatches on accounts `-2` / `-1` (AC4). One night's cheap window is enough to show the mechanism engages, not enough to estimate a steady-state paid-spend rate — do not read the 16.6% overlap token figure as a recurring cost.
- `low_priority_sessions` from the CLI reads **0** in both post-change windows and 13 in the baseline: that column buckets by the retired fast/cheap **mode schedule**, which the config no longer defines (cheap hours are now a priority cap, not a mode). Use `priority_routing`/`priority_decision` counts instead — which is what this report does.
- Aggregate `rate_limited` (−23%) and `fallback_after_queue` (−92%) moved favourably, `empty_response` (+70) and upstream 503 (+25, all `opencode-go`) moved unfavourably; with seven other changes in-window these deltas are **not** attributable to the low-chain change alone.

### Verdict

The 5-entry low chain **does** absorb low-priority overflow into `opencode-go-3`/`-2` inside the off-peak windows (915 fallbacks, 1,806 dispatches, 137.2 M tokens), does **not** widen paid spend in the gap windows beyond one boundary event (2 dispatches, 0.006% of tokens — bug filed), per-key failover is exercised (`-2` used; `-1` blocked only by exhausted quota), and the free tier's relative share fell as designed (`munitoai-free` lines −59%) without any evidence of a low-chain cost leak.

# Plan: Per model context size — decomposition

Decomposed into 5 child items (test-first ordering), <work-item-id>. Effort Small / Risk Medium; approval gate (`plan-approval-gate`) returned `request_approval: false`, so no approval pause is needed.

## Feature plan

### F1 — Per-entry context-limit tests (task, test-first)
**Summary:** Add the failing test coverage for the per-entry `max_context_tokens` gate before any implementation lands.
**Minimal implementation:** new `proxy/tests/test_provider_context_limit.py`; extend `proxy/tests/test_provider_fallback.py` and `proxy/tests/test_munitoai_fallback_chain.py`; tests assert against the agreed `max_context_tokens` / `provider_context_exceeded` vocabulary.
**Dependencies:** none (first). **Deliverables:** red tests + config-parse pinning.

### F2 — Implement `max_context_tokens` gate (feature)
**Summary:** Add the optional per-entry field, a reader + gate helper in `proxy/provider.py`, and enforce the skip in both fallback loops before `acquire_provider_budget`/dispatch.
**Minimal implementation:** `_provider_context_limit()` reader; `_should_skip_provider_context()` helper; extract the shared estimate (tokenizer + `_estimate_effective_prompt_tokens_for_routing` + multiplier) into one per-request computation reusable by both cycles; fold the limit into the local branch as an additional hard cap (`min(existing thresholds, limit)`); record attempt status `provider_context_exceeded`; no cooldown/affinity/usage-limit/queue side effects.
**Dependencies:** F1. **Deliverables:** gate code + attempt/log plumbing; F1 green.

### F3 — Ship sourced config limits (feature)
**Summary:** Set documented, sourced `max_context_tokens` on the remote entries with meaningful ceilings (`munitoai-free`, `munitoai`, `opencode-go*`, `deepseek-flash`); leave ungated anything unsourceable.
**Minimal implementation:** `proxy/config.yaml` edits with source comments; keep ≥1 remote tier effectively ungated (deepseek-flash at its upstream window) so the chain never exhausts for oversized prompts; config-parse tests pass against shipped values.
**Dependencies:** F2. **Deliverables:** shipped config + pinned parse tests.

### F4 — Docs and observability (feature)
**Summary:** Reflect the new field semantics and skip behaviour in the field tables and routing docs; register `provider_context_exceeded` as a backend-signal counter.
**Minimal implementation:** `proxy/MODEL_ADD.md` field table, `proxy/README.md`, `proxy/docs/routing.md` semantics + skip-behaviour table; `proxy/observability.py` counter (mirroring `context_too_large`).
**Dependencies:** F2, F3. **Deliverables:** updated docs + counter.

### F5 — Full-suite green gate (task, verification)
**Summary:** Confirm no regressions: full project suite + audit across the change.
**Minimal implementation:** run the suite via the test skill; fix any regressions in-scope; doc/code consistency check.
**Dependencies:** F1–F4. **Deliverables:** green suite + audit record.

## AC traceability (parent → children)
- Parent AC1 (config field + absent/0 disabled) → F2-AC1, F3 (parse pinning)
- Parent AC2 (skip before budget in both loops) → F2-AC2
- Parent AC3 (attempt status + log) → F2-AC3, F4-AC2
- Parent AC4 (estimate reuse) → F2-AC4
- Parent AC5 (skip ≠ failure) → F2-AC5
- Parent AC6 (queue-safe) → F2-AC6
- Parent AC7 (local composes as extra cap) → F2-AC7
- Parent AC8 (shipped sourced values) → F3-AC1
- Parent AC9 (test coverage) → F1-AC1
- Parent AC10 (docs) → F4-AC1
- Parent AC11 (full suite) → F5-AC1

## Vertical-slice phasing decision
Item is effort **Small**; full 3-12-phase vertical-slice phasing is not warranted. Children are functional slices ordered test-first (tests → gate → config → docs/obs → verification), and F2 is itself a vertical slice through config parsing, routing, and dispatch.

## Appendix: clarifying questions & answers (plan session)
Recorded plan decisions; no question was routed to the producer (unattended dispatch; recommended options applied and documented, per plan-skill defaulting rules). Any residual open question is re-raised at the relevant implementation child.

- **Q (self-resolved): Final field name.** `max_context_tokens` (working name, pervasive in the intake brief, ACs and constraints) vs `context_size` vs `max_prompt_tokens`. Recommended: **`max_context_tokens`** — applied consistently across config, code, logs and docs. Evidence: brief Constraints/Naming + AC wording.
- **Q (self-resolved): New skip status name.** Recommended: **`provider_context_exceeded`** recorded via `_record_attempt` with `estimated_tokens`, `limit` and `reason`, plus a routing log line. Evidence: `_record_attempt` diagnostics (proxy/provider.py:4909), `context_too_large` precedent.
- **Q (self-resolved): Where the gate lives.** Recommended: one gate helper checked once per provider entry inside both `_proxy_with_remote_fallback_cycle` and `_proxy_with_fallback_cycle`, immediately after `_resolve_provider_with_exclusions` and **before** `acquire_provider_budget`. Evidence: chain loop structure (proxy/provider.py:6227, 6809) and `_should_skip_local` precedent (proxy/provider.py:1894).
- **Q (self-resolved): Estimate cost / single pass.** Recommended: compute the routing estimate **once per request** (per cycle), reusing `_get_tokenizer_for_model` + `_estimate_effective_prompt_tokens_for_routing` + `token_estimate_multiplier`; refactor the estimate block already inline in `_proxy_with_fallback_cycle` into a shared helper so the remote-only cycle reuses it (no duplicate tokenizer pass per provider). Evidence: proxy/provider.py:7070-7078, brief Constraint/Estimate reuse + AC4.
- **Q (self-resolved): Local composition semantics.** Recommended: for a local entry, `max_context_tokens` is folded into the existing local gate as an extra hard cap — effective warm cap = `min(effective_per_slot_threshold(...), max_context_tokens)` — never loosening current behaviour. Evidence: AC7 + `_should_skip_local` / `_effective_large_context_thresholds`.
- **Q (self-resolved): Shipped values — chain-exhaustion guard.** Recommended: source each value from the upstream model context window or the provider's documented per-minute token allowance; keep `deepseek-flash` (the final remote tier) at its upstream window so a very large prompt still has an ungated-ish destination and the chain cannot exhaust solely due to caps. Unsourceable values are left unset with an open question rather than guessed. Evidence: brief Constraint/Values + Risks/chain-exhaustion; open question forwarded to F3.
- **Q (self-resolved): Observability scope.** Recommended: add `provider_context_exceeded` to `backend_signal_counts` (mirroring `context_too_large`) in addition to per-request attempts + logs, so operators can watch skip volume. Evidence: proxy/observability.py:78; brief Key Files mention.
